# Intelli Search for DeepSeek Harness [_DeepSeek Harness_](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`) host bundle for [`@curio-data/mcp-intelli-search`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@curio-data/mcp-intelli-search): intelligent web research with a five-stage pipeline (search, fetch, per-page extraction, collation, cache suggestions), cited answers and a local `.search/` cache of every run. The bundle adds two entries to a harness profile. One starts the standalone MCP server through `npx` with `--host dsh`; the other registers the shared `intelli-search` skill. The generator pins the server version in the launcher. Search and research run in that server, not in the bundle. ## Requirements - `dsh` within the declared `engines.dsh` range `>=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0` (see Evidence and Limits below) - [_Node.js_](https://nodejs.org/) 24.9 or later on `PATH` (the harness's own floor; the first start downloads the MCP package through `npx`) - For installation and removal, `pnpm` on `PATH` or an explicit `pnpmCommand`. A launcher-provided package manager takes precedence. - An [_OpenRouter_](https://openrouter.ai) API key for the search, extract and collate stages ## Installation Installation by name requires both this package and its matching MCP server on npm. Install into the profile used to start the harness (`tui` in this example): ```bash dsh plugin --profile tui add @curio-data/dsh-intelli-search ``` Start the same profile from the project directory with `dsh --profile tui`. ## Credentials The server receives its key through the harness environment layer. Precedence: an `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` exported in the launching environment, then a `.env` file in the launch directory, then `$DSH_HOME/.env`. Accepted values are copied into the environment once at launch, so restart that profile after changing a key. To use the key across launching shells, prepare the harness-home file before entering the key: ```bash (umask 077; touch "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/.env") && chmod 600 "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/.env" ``` After the command succeeds, open the file in an editor so the key stays out of shell history. Put `OPENROUTER_API_KEY=` on its own line, replacing any previous definition. The bridge row forwards `process.env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY` to the server; the server treats an empty value as absent and starts without a key. A key stored through the harness model-settings page does not provision this server: that credential is resolved through a service a child process cannot read. Alternatively, `npx -y --package @curio-data/mcp-intelli-search mcp-intelli-search setup` reads a key from standard input and stores it in a user-only credential file beside the per-user configuration at `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/mcp-intelli-search` (shared with the Codex host mode). A stored file is reread on each call; a nonempty environment key takes precedence. Remove `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` from all three environment layers and restart to use the file. ## Workspace and Cache The server uses the harness working directory as its workspace and writes the research cache (`.search/` by default) below it. Start the harness from the project directory: a directory change later in the session does not move the cache. For a fixed project root, override the row with id `mcp-intelli-search` in `$DSH_HOME/profiles//cordis.patch.yml` and set `cwd`. The override replaces that row's entire `config`. Copy its other `config` fields from the bundle and update the pinned package version after each bundle upgrade. A home or filesystem-root working directory is rejected with an actionable `WORKSPACE` error instead of creating an accidental shared cache. ## Tools and Timeouts The harness names the MCP server `intelli`, so the four tools appear as: - `mcp__intelli__intelli_search` - `mcp__intelli__intelli_extract` - `mcp__intelli__intelli_collate` - `mcp__intelli__intelli_research` Start with `intelli_search` for quick facts; `intelli_research` runs the full pipeline over multiple pages. Research calls can take minutes: the bundle raises the bridge call limit to ten minutes (`toolCallTimeoutMs: 600000`). Server startup and tool discovery use a separate request timeout (60 seconds on `0.2.2-rc.1`), so a slow first `npx` download can still lose the tools on a first start; a later start reuses the `npx` cache. A missing tool set means the bridge row did not start. The bundle sets `failOnStartupError: false`, so the harness keeps running and logs the failure rather than surfacing it: report the missing tools together with the startup log instead of substituting the harness's own web search. On `0.2.2-rc.1`, a project skill with the same name outranks the bundle's skill registration; a user-level skill does not. ## Verification After restarting with a key in place, request a quick search with `mcp__intelli__intelli_search` and confirm an actual tool call and an answer with sources. A running harness and a registered tool list do not prove provider access. `dsh --profile --dump-config` shows the composed bundle rows, with `!!js` expressions verbatim, and is the first check when tools are missing. ## Removal ```bash dsh plugin --profile remove @curio-data/dsh-intelli-search ``` Restart the same profile with `dsh --profile `, then confirm with `dsh --profile --dump-config` that the two bundle rows are gone. ## Evidence and Limits Installation, exact tool registration, skill loading, workspace guards, credential-free startup and dummy credential delivery are verified against `dsh` `0.2.2-rc.1` and `0.2.2-rc.5` on Linux with the local bundle and no provider calls. Credentialed local-bundle search, research and credential-file fallback were verified separately on `0.2.2-rc.1` only. The whole declared range and registry-pin installation have not been tested. ## Licence Apache-2.0. Copyright 2026 Ashraf Miah, Curio Data Pro Ltd. See `LICENSE`. This package bundles no third-party code, so it carries no `NOTICE`. The MCP server it launches through `npx`, `@curio-data/mcp-intelli-search`, ships its own `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`. # pi-intelli-search [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@curio-data/pi-intelli-search?color=blue)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@curio-data/pi-intelli-search) [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/@curio-data/pi-intelli-search?color=blue)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@curio-data/pi-intelli-search) [![pi compatible](https://img.shields.io/badge/pi-%E2%89%A50.86.0-blueviolet)](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-green)](./LICENSE) ![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/test%3Aall-1184%20passing-brightgreen) Intelligent web research for coding agents: search, extract, collate, and cache grounded web context in one tool call.

**DeepSeek Harness profile plugin:** bring cited web search and multi-page research into [_DeepSeek Harness_](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Ask for a quick fact with sources, or compare several pages and keep the report and its sources in the project. Install into the `tui` profile with `dsh plugin --profile tui add @curio-data/dsh-intelli-search`. See [profile setup and verification](#deepseek-harness) for credentials and other profile names. **Features:** - 🔍 **Search:** a search-grounded model, [_Perplexity Sonar_](https://docs.perplexity.ai) via [_OpenRouter_](https://openrouter.ai) by default. One application programming interface (API) key, no $50 minimum. Chat models with tool support also work through the web search server tool; see [native search settings](#openrouter-web-search-server-tool) or [Model Context Protocol (MCP) tuning](#tuning). - 🔗 **Harvest:** provider-supplied citation links recovered from the response, alongside links in the answer. Recognised `url_citation` annotations are merged with text links before pages are selected; recovery is best-effort, not a complete record of sources consulted. - 🌐 **Fetch:** Dual-fetch each page (Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) → [_Defuddle_](https://github.com/kepano/defuddle) versus Markdown endpoint), compare quality, pick the cleaner version. - 📄 **Extract:** Per-page large language model (LLM) extraction guided by a _focused prompt_. Compresses ≈50K to ≈3-5K chars of query-relevant content. - 🔗 **Collate:** Cross-source deduplication, inconsistency detection, and synthesis into a focused ≈5K-character summary. - 📚 **Batch Research:** One `intelli_research` call accepts two or more questions known at launch (up to ten by default) and returns either a separate answer for each (independent mode) or one merged report on a common topic (expansion mode). The entries run concurrently, four at a time by default, and the agent receives every answer in one result instead of making one call per question. In one paired benchmark on the native `Pi` host, a session that submitted five questions on one topic as one expansion batch used ≈74% less main-model input and finished ≈63% sooner than a session making five separate calls. The main-model charge fell ≈25%, because most of the separate calls' input was cached context billed below the full input price. That is one pair on one topic, not a general result. Batching follows observed use: in a survey of one host's agent transcripts, 39% of `Pi` messages calling `intelli_research` issued two to five calls, and 15 of 30 sampled follow-up calls made within five minutes were steps the agent had already planned. See [Planned Research Questions](#planned-research-questions), the [benchmark](docs/BENCHMARKS.md#batch-research-on-the-native-host) and the [survey](docs/proposals/BATCH-RESEARCH.md#evidence). - 🧠 **Reasoning-Aware Output Budget:** When a reasoning model spends its output cap on hidden reasoning, research retries at a doubled cap (8,000, then 16,000, then 32,000 tokens by default) before reporting a failure. See [Output Budget Retry](#output-budget-retry). - 📏 **Long Pages, Bounded Collation:** Extraction reads up to 400,000 characters of each page. When the extractions exceed the [collation input budget](#collation-input-budget), the longest are trimmed at clean boundaries, and the result gives the path of each trimmed extraction's full saved file. - 🧾 **Recoverable Failures:** When no extraction succeeds, research saves the fetched pages and a failure report; when synthesis fails, it saves the pages and extractions as well. The result names the saved files, so the agent can read them rather than repeat the paid stages. See [Extraction Diagnostics](#extraction-diagnostics). - 📂 **Code and Text Sources:** Raw source files and text responses are saved and extracted alongside HTML pages. References named in search text without a link are fetched as labelled guesses; see [Inferred Assets](#inferred-assets). - 💾 **Cache:** Persistent `.search/` cache with automatic cache suggest. Related previous searches surfaced on each query. - 🎯 **Configurable:** Select models independently for search, extract and collate. The native extension uses registered, authenticated `Pi` models (capability and context limits apply); the MCP server uses explicitly selected OpenRouter models. - 💰 **Cost:** see the [default research-run estimate](#cost). Two packages run the research engine; a third, `@curio-data/dsh-intelli-search`, connects DeepSeek Harness to the standalone server: - `@curio-data/pi-intelli-search`: a [`Pi`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) extension that registers the four research tools natively, using `Pi` settings, authentication and the model registry. - `@curio-data/mcp-intelli-search`: a standalone Model Context Protocol (MCP) server over standard input/output (stdio) for MCP-compatible hosts, including [_Claude Code_](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp) and [_Codex_](https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp). Both packages run the same five-stage pipeline with the same cache format. [Install](#install) covers both the [`Pi` native extension](#pi-native-extension) and the [MCP server](#mcp-server), including direct MCP registration and host plugins. The shared pipeline searches via a search-grounded model ([_Perplexity Sonar_](https://docs.perplexity.ai), the native default) and merges prose links with harvested citations before selecting pages. It fetches pages through a dual-fetch comparison ([_Defuddle_](https://github.com/kepano/defuddle) versus Markdown endpoint), then extracts query-relevant content per page with a dedicated large language model (LLM) guided by a _focused prompt_. Collation deduplicates findings, flags inconsistencies, and synthesises a concise summary. Reports, extractions and fetched content are cached for offline reuse in `.search/` by default. Cache suggest surfaces related previous searches on each query. ## Three Packages, One Engine Choose the installation route for the host: | Route | Host | What to Install | |---|---|---| | Native `Pi` Extension | `Pi` | `@curio-data/pi-intelli-search` | | Direct MCP Registration | Any MCP-compatible host | `@curio-data/mcp-intelli-search` | | Host Plugin | Claude Code or Codex | Repository marketplace launching the pinned MCP package | | Host Plugin | DeepSeek Harness | Profile bundle `@curio-data/dsh-intelli-search`; installation by name requires its matching MCP release. | The install branches: [`Pi` Native Extension](#pi-native-extension) and [MCP Server](#mcp-server), with host instructions for [Claude Code](#claude-code), [Codex](#codex), [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/Curio-Data/pi-intelli-search/blob/mcp-v0.25.0/README.md#deepseek-harness) and any [Generic MCP Host](#generic-mcp-host). The native extension uses `Pi` settings and authentication. Generic MCP registration requires explicit configuration and a workspace; the Codex and DeepSeek Harness launchers take the workspace from the host working directory and use built-in defaults unless a per-user configuration is supplied. Inference uses an OpenRouter key supplied through the configured environment variable or credential file. The MCP server does not read `Pi` settings or credentials. ## Contents - [Three Packages, One Engine](#three-packages-one-engine) - [Install](#install) - [`Pi` Native Extension](#pi-native-extension) - [Provenance](#provenance) - [Sponsor](#sponsor) - [Licence](#licence) - [Use of Large Language Models](#use-of-large-language-models) ## Install Choose a package by host: the [`Pi` native extension](#pi-native-extension) for `Pi`, or the [MCP server](#mcp-server) for MCP-compatible hosts. ### `Pi` Native Extension #### Prerequisites Install `Pi` >= 0.86.0 and obtain an [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai) account. One key covers search, extraction and collation with the default models. Other providers are supported for extraction and collation; see [Model Configuration](#model-configuration). 1. **Sign In With OAuth (Recommended):** run `/login openrouter` in `Pi`. On `Pi` 0.82.0 and later this performs OpenRouter OAuth Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) sign-in and stores a user-controlled key automatically. No manual key paste is required. 2. **Or add a key manually:** create one at [openrouter.ai/keys](https://openrouter.ai/keys), then edit `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`: ```json { "openrouter": { "type": "api_key", "key": "sk-or-v1-..." } } ``` #### Install the Extension From `npm` (recommended): ```bash pi install npm:@curio-data/pi-intelli-search ``` From _GitHub_: ```bash pi install git:github.com/Curio-Data/pi-intelli-search ``` Local development: ```bash pi install /path/to/pi-intelli-search ``` On first load, `Pi` shows `Added models:` followed by any missing models: on a fresh install these are `perplexity/sonar`, `perplexity/sonar-pro`, and `perplexity/sonar-pro-search`. An upgrade lists only models not already registered. A missing OpenRouter key produces a warning notification. #### Verify Installation Start `Pi` and type `/model`. Confirm that `perplexity/sonar`, `perplexity/sonar-pro`, and `perplexity/sonar-pro-search` appear in the model list. If they are missing after a manual edit, reopen `/model`: since `Pi` 0.82.0 the picker reloads `models.json` on open. Restart `Pi` only if they are still absent. Registration does not select a pipeline model; `searchModel` in settings does that. #### Release Notes After an Update On `Pi` 1.5.0 and later, the next fresh launch after a package update shows newer package release notes under Extension Updates. The first time `Pi` sees the package, it records the version without showing release notes. Notes come from [`PI_CHANGELOG.md`](PI_CHANGELOG.md), a native-only changelog generated from the canonical [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and declared to the host through `pi.changelogPath`. Hosts before 1.5.0 ignore the field and the file, so the package behaves the same on the supported floor of `Pi` 0.86.0. Set the top-level `Pi` setting `collapseChangelog` to `true` in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` to show one line per updated package. #### Customise (Optional) No configuration is needed to get started. The defaults use OpenRouter for all stages. To limit research to six pages, add this block to `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` or, for a trusted project, `/.pi/settings.json`: ```json { "$schema": "https://pi.dev/schemas/settings.schema.json", "pi-intelli-search": { "defaultUrls": 6, "maxUrls": 6 } } ``` `Pi` 1.2.0 publishes the [settings schema](https://pi.dev/schemas/settings.schema.json) referenced by the optional `$schema` line. It provides editor validation and completion for host settings and permits the `pi-intelli-search` namespace without validating or completing its keys. The published [models schema](https://pi.dev/schemas/models.schema.json) accepts the Sonar registrations the extension writes. See [Model Configuration](#model-configuration) for model selection, [Configuration Recipes](#configuration-recipes) for complete examples, and [Settings](#settings) for defaults and the full reference. ### MCP Server `@curio-data/mcp-intelli-search` serves the four research tools over stdio. The Claude Code example below covers configuration, credentials, registration and verification in one sequence. Host plugins and generic registration follow as alternatives; install only one route in a host to avoid duplicate tool sets. #### MCP Prerequisites - [_Node.js_](https://nodejs.org/) 22 or later for the standalone package, with `node` and `npx` on `PATH`. The [DeepSeek Harness](#deepseek-harness) bundle follows that host's own floor, Node.js 24.9 or later. - [_Claude Code_](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) installed for the example below. - An [OpenRouter API key](https://openrouter.ai/keys) with credit for inference. One key covers all three model roles; charges are separate from the host subscription. - An existing project folder for the research cache. The server and host must be able to read the same filesystem. Generic registration requires an explicit JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) configuration and absolute workspace path. The Codex and DeepSeek Harness launchers use the host working directory and built-in model defaults when no per-user configuration exists. The server reads no host credential stores, `Pi` settings or discovered project configuration. Native fetch assets are verified on _Linux_ x86-64; _macOS_ and _Windows_ are not verified. See [Compatibility](#mcp-server-compatibility) for the recorded scope. #### Claude Code Run the following steps from the project folder in a [_Bash_](https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/) shell. Direct registration is private to the operator and active only in that folder. ##### Create the Configuration Save this as `.intelli-search.json` in the project folder: ```json { "providers": { "openrouter": { "apiKeyEnv": "OPENROUTER_API_KEY" } }, "models": { "search": { "provider": "openrouter", "model": "perplexity/sonar" }, "extract": { "provider": "openrouter", "model": "minimax/minimax-m3" }, "collate": { "provider": "openrouter", "model": "minimax/minimax-m3" } } } ``` These are explicit model selections, not inherited defaults. The configuration contains the credential variable's name, not the key itself. The cache lands in the project folder's `.search/` directory. ##### Supply the API Key Enter the key at the hidden prompt, rather than writing it into shell history or a configuration file: ```bash read -r -s -p 'OpenRouter API key: ' OPENROUTER_API_KEY printf '\n' export OPENROUTER_API_KEY ``` The export lasts for this shell session. Launch Claude Code from this shell so its server inherits the key. Repeat this step in a new shell, or use a secret manager to supply the variable. Restart Claude Code after changing the key; the server snapshots credentials at startup. ##### Register the Server ```bash claude mcp add intelli_search --scope local \ -e "INTELLI_SEARCH_CONFIG=$PWD/.intelli-search.json" \ -e "INTELLI_SEARCH_WORKSPACE=$PWD" \ -- npx -y --package @curio-data/mcp-intelli-search \ mcp-intelli-search ``` `npx` downloads the package on first use; no separate package installation is required. Append `@` to the package name to pin a release. The command records absolute paths for this folder. Replace `--scope local` with `--scope project` only to share registration through `.mcp.json`; project-scoped servers require approval, and those paths must exist on each operator's machine. Never put the API key in that file. ##### Verify the Connection Validate the configuration and workspace: ```bash npx -y --package @curio-data/mcp-intelli-search \ mcp-intelli-search \ --config "$PWD/.intelli-search.json" \ --workspace "$PWD" \ --check-config ``` A successful check prints `Configuration is valid.` and exits with status `0`. This check requires no credentials and performs no inference; it does not test model access. Check the registered server, then start a session from the same shell: ```bash claude mcp list claude ``` Confirm `intelli_search` shows as connected. In the session, run `/mcp` to inspect its four tools: `intelli_search`, `intelli_extract`, `intelli_collate` and `intelli_research`. To test inference, ask: “Use intelli_search to find the current TypeScript release and cite the official source.” This call incurs OpenRouter charges. A successful answer with sources verifies inference separately from the connection check. ##### Customise the Server Change the model selections in `.intelli-search.json`, or add an optional `tuning` object alongside `providers` and `models`. For example, `"tuning": { "defaultUrls": 6, "maxUrls": 6 }` limits research to six pages. Restart the host after changes. See [Configuration](#configuration) and [Tuning](#tuning) for the full reference. #### Claude Code Plugin The [Claude Code plugin](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins) bundles the server registration and an agent-facing research skill. Use it instead of direct registration: ```bash claude plugin marketplace add Curio-Data/pi-intelli-search claude plugin install intelli-search@curio-data-plugins ``` Set the required `openrouter_api_key` option through `/plugin` → Installed → `intelli-search` → Configure. Claude Code stores it in its credential store and withholds the server until it is set. Unlike direct registration, this plugin ignores an exported `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`: the plugin option supplies that variable. Create the plugin data directory: ```bash mkdir -p "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/plugins/data/intelli-search-curio-data-plugins" ``` Save the same [minimal configuration](#create-the-configuration) as `config.json` in that directory. It persists across plugin updates but is removed on uninstall. The launcher uses the opened project as its workspace, so each project's cache stays in its own `.search/` di

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# ComfyUI Chenxin Preset

DSH 预设：3 个 camera 技能 + 1 个提示词创作插件（prompt-forge）+ 共享运行时，让 agent 在本机 ComfyUI 上完成 Anima / MiniMax H3 提示词编写与生图生视频。

![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/cxin21/dsh-comfyui-chenxin)
![GitHub license](https://img.shields.io/github/license/cxin21/dsh-comfyui-chenxin)
![GitHub release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/cxin21/dsh-comfyui-chenxin)
![GitHub last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/cxin21/dsh-comfyui-chenxin)
![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/Platform-Windows-blue)
![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-Agent%20Preset-8A2BE2)

## ✨ 功能亮点

- **3 个开箱即用的 camera CLI 技能 + 提示词创作插件**：生图 + 生视频 + 多视图角色卡；Anima / MiniMax H3 提示词编写由 prompt-forge 插件承担
- **Anima 文生图 / 图生图**：`camera-image`（t2i / i2i），pinned 工作流零配置
- **MiniMax H3 视频**：`camera-video`（t2v / i2v / multi-i2v），支持跨段参考图与参考音频
- **多视图角色卡**：`camera-multiview`（Flux2-Klein），一张卡出多视角
- **统一 P1 Envelope**：所有 CLI 输出结构一致，agent / 脚本都好解析
- **幂等一键安装**：`scripts/setup.ps1` 自动建 venv、装依赖、自检 3 个 CLI

## 5 分钟跑起来

```powershell
# 一次性：装 Python 3.10+，把 preset 拿到本地，然后：
git clone https://github.com/cxin21/dsh-comfyui-chenxin.git
# 从 GitHub Releases (v0.1.0) 下载 3 个数据包（.gz），解压后放回：
#   assets/knowledge/anima-prompt-v1/tag-catalog.sqlite   （来自 tag-catalog.sqlite.gz）
#   assets/knowledge/anima-prompt-v1/tags.sqlite          （来自 tags.sqlite.gz）
#   assets/knowledge/minimax-h3-prompt/tokenizer.json     （来自 tokenizer.json.gz）
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/setup.ps1

# 重启 DSH，会话起来后 loader 会自动注册 3 个 CLI 工具
# （camera_image / camera_video / camera_multiview）；提示词创作由 prompt-forge 插件承担
```

> **大文件不走 git**：三个知识库快照（共 ~993 MB）体积过大，托管在
> [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/cxin21/dsh-comfyui-chenxin/releases)（tag `v0.1.0`，
> gzip 压缩后共 ~241 MB）。clone 后按上表放回路径即可，仓库内 `.gitignore` 已排除它们。

`scripts/setup.ps1` 会创建 `<preset>/.venv`、装 `tokenizers`、把 6 个本地包装进 venv、自检 3 个 CLI，全部幂等。详见 `docs/development.md`。

### 让 DSH 认到这个 preset

DSH 只通过 **bundle** 装载预设（`plugin_manager` 装一个声明了 `dsh.bundle.patch` 的包）。仓库里两份装配文件的分工是：

| 文件 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | bundle 声明，`dsh.bundle.patch` 指向 `cordis.patch.yml` |
| `agent.cordis.yml` | **可移植的源**，供人编辑与评审；plugin `name` 写 `./` 相对路径，`presetRoot` 写 `null` |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | **DSH 真正加载的部署产物**，由 `scripts/render_patch.py` 从源生成，**不要手改** |
| `scripts/render_patch.py` | 把源里的 3 个部署字段重写成**本机 checkout 的绝对路径** |

**为什么 patch 必须带本机绝对路径**：DSH 挂载 preset 时，嵌套 plugin entry 是从 **host 侧 base**（asar 里的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` / `dsh-app-boot`）import 的，不是从 profile 目录。在这个解析链里：

- `./loader.js` —— dsh-app-boot 的 `anchorInsertedPluginNames` 只在 `entry.group && Array.isArray(entry.config)` 时递归进 config，本 preset 行是普通 object config，嵌套的 `./` 不锚定，以字面量按 profile 目录解析 → 失败；
- `@local/dsh-comfyui-chenxin-preset/loader.js` —— 这个包链接只在 **profile 的** `node_modules` 里，host 侧 base 下 `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`，Loader 吞掉错误 → 预设条目 `never started`，在菜单里直接消失；
- `file:///<本机 checkout>/loader.js` —— 所有 base 下都能解析。

实测证据见 `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md` #29。所以 patch 里的这 3 项是按机器生成的，不能入库一份死路径，也不能硬编码别人的路径。

**正确工作流**：只编辑 `agent.cordis.yml`（源，不含机器路径），然后跑

```powershell
python scripts/render_patch.py          # 从源重新生成 cordis.patch.yml（3 个本机绝对路径）
python scripts/check_lockstep.py        # 校验 patch 是源的正确部署
```

`setup.ps1` / `setup.sh` 会自动跑 `render_patch.py`，所以换机器 clone 后跑一次 setup 即可；不要把 `cordis.patch.yml` 手工改回相对路径或子路径。

需要按机器覆盖的其它配置写进 profile 自己的 `cordis.patch.yml`（user 层），不要写进仓库。

`check_lockstep.py` 断言五件事：源与 patch 的 entry 列表除 **3 个允许的部署重写**外逐条相同、源不含机器路径、patch 的绝对路径全部指向**本 checkout**、每个入口在磁盘上真实存在、`preset.yml` 的 name/description 与 patch 一致。3 个允许的重写是：

1. `comfyui-loader.name`：`./loader.js` → `file:///<checkout>/loader.js`
2. `comfyui-loader.config.presetRoot`：`null` → `<checkout>`
3. `prompt-forge.name`：`./plugins/...` → `file:///<checkout>/plugins/...`

为什么这条要紧：**DSH 读的是 `cordis.patch.yml`**，`agent.cordis.yml` 只是源；两者漂移时，你改的东西不会生效，而不改的东西会生效。

> **`plugins/prompt-forge/dist/` 不入 git**（构建产物）。所以全新 clone 里 patch 指向的入口文件还不存在，而 dsh-app-boot 会把 bundle 加载失败静默塞进 `skippedBundles`（不打印任何东西）——表现是「预设起来了但没有 prompt-forge 工具」。`scripts/setup.ps1` / `setup.sh` 现在会在第 5 步自动 `npm ci && npm run build`；如果你跳过了 setup，手动跑一次 `cd plugins/prompt-forge && npm ci && npm run build`。

> 旧版 DSH 用 `$DSH_HOME/.agent-presets/<id>/` 目录装载（`preset.yml` + `agent.cordis.yml`）。**那个目录现在没有任何代码读取**，所以本仓库不再提供该形态的安装步骤；`agent.cordis.yml` 保留只是为了可读性 + 锁步 gate。

装成 bundle 一次即可，装完 profile 的 `package.json` 里 `dsh.profile.bundles` 会多一项，重启 DSH 后新会话可在预设菜单里选 `ComfyUI Chenxin`：

- **Desktop**：侧栏 **Plugins** 页面 → **Add plugin**，填入本 checkout 的绝对路径 → 安装后 **Enable now**。或对 agent 说「用 plugin_manager 安装 `link:<checkout 绝对路径>`」。桌面端的 profile 由 Electron 拥有，`dsh plugin` 命令会拒绝管理它（设置里的 **Built-in plugins** 只是只读清单）。
- **命令行 profile**：`dsh plugin --profile <name> add link:<checkout 绝对路径>`（需 pnpm 在 `PATH` 上）。

`link:` 意味着改源码后要重新构建（`cd plugins/prompt-forge && npm run build`）并重启才生效；它用这个 checkout 的依赖，不会另装一份。安装 bundle 会在 Host 进程里执行插件代码，需要 Full access 或一次批准。

## 这是什么

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  agent ──► loader.js ──► ctx.skills (catalog) + ctx.tools (3 个 CLI)   │
│                                                                      │
│  plugins/prompt-forge  ← 提示词创作内核（Anima/H3 编译+审计+管理）    │
│  assets/knowledge/      ← 知识资产（tag-catalog/tags/tokenizer 等）   │
│  skills/camera-image    ← Anima camera workflow（t2i/i2i）            │
│  skills/camera-video    ← MiniMax H3 视频（t2v/i2v/multi-i2v）        │
│  skills/camera-multiview← Flux2-Klein 多视图角色卡                  │
│                                                                      │
│  runtime/chenxin_runtime   ← P1 envelope + 共享 CLI runner + 相机引擎 │
│  runtime/comfyui_http      ← stdlib HTTP 通道（history/view）          │
│  runtime/comfyui_mcp       ← comfyui-mcp stdio JSON-RPC 客户端         │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

3 个 runtime 包是 Python 源码（不是 wheel），通过 `.pth` + distlib launchers 直接装进 venv——绕开 `pip install -e` 的构建路径（在那台 Windows 机器上会稳定报错）。详见 `docs/architecture.md`。

## 给谁用、什么时候调哪个 skill

| 我想做 | 用这个 | 然后用 |
|---|---|---|
| 写 Anima 提示词（slot → 单行 positive/negative） | `prompt_author` (target=anima) / `prompt_compile`（prompt-forge 插件） | `camera-image` |
| 写 MiniMax H3 视频提示词（T2VA / I2VA / FL2VA / L2VA / Ref2VA） | `prompt_author` (target=h3) / `prompt_compile`（prompt-forge 插件） | `camera-video` |
| 跑 Anima 图（text→image / image→image） | `camera-image` | — |
| 跑 MiniMax H3 视频 | `camera-video` | — |
| 跑多视图角色卡（Flux2-Klein） | `camera-multiview` | — |

完整决策树见 `AGENTS.md`。

## 仓库结构

```
.
├── README.md                            ← 本文件
├── AGENTS.md                            ← agent 工作守则
├── preset.yml                           ← loader 注册元数据
├── package.json                         ← DSH bundle 声明（指向 cordis.patch.yml）
├── loader.js                            ← DSH 插件入口
├── agent.cordis.yml                     ← Cordis 组合配置（可移植形态）
├── cordis.patch.yml                     ← 同一组合的部署形态（bundle 消费）
├── requirements.lock                    ← 第三方依赖钉版（17 个包）
├── scripts/
│   ├── setup.ps1                        ← 一键安装（幂等）
│   ├── setup.sh                         ← 同上，POSIX
│   ├── install_local.py                 ← 绕开 pip 的本地包安装器
│   ├── check_contracts.py               ← SKILL.md 契约 gate
│   ├── check_loader.mjs                 ← loader 接线 / 失败域隔离 gate
│   └── check_lockstep.py                ← agent.cordis.yml ↔ cordis.patch.yml 一致性 gate
├── docs/
│   ├── architecture.md                  ← 设计原理与契约
│   ├── cli-cookbook.md                  ← 每个 CLI 的完整使用手册
│   ├── development.md                   ← setup / install_local / 调试
│   └── troubleshooting.md               ← 常见错误与恢复
├── temp/                                ← 运行时生成物（可按技能子目录清理）
│   ├── anima-prompt-v1/                 ← relation-overlay.sqlite（catalog_relations）
│   ├── camera-image/                    ← t2i/i2i 产物 PNG + summary.json
│   ├── camera-video/                    ← t2v/i2v/multi-i2v 产物 mp4 + summary.json
│   ├── camera-multiview/                ← 多视图 PNG + summary.json
│   └── runtime/.workflow_cache/         ← 引擎缓存（10-deep LRU）
├── data/
│   └── runtime/                         ← prompt_feedback 反馈记录（feedback.sqlite）
├── assets/knowledge/                    ← 知识资产（prompt-forge 只读消费）
│   ├── anima-prompt-v1/                 ← tag-catalog.sqlite / tags.sqlite / manifest.json
│   └── minimax-h3-prompt/               ← tokenizer.json / tokenizer_config.json / chat_template.json
├── plugins/prompt-forge/               ← 提示词创作内核（编译+审计+管理工具）
├── skills/
│   ├── camera-image/
│   │   ├── SKILL.md
│   │   └── camera_image/runtime/        ← 请求解析 / graph / assets
│   ├── camera-video/
│   │   ├── SKILL.md
│   │   └── camera_video/runtime/
│   └── camera-multiview/
│       ├── SKILL.md
│       ├── camera_multiview/
│       └── references/
└── runtime/
    ├── chenxin_runtime/                 ← P1 envelope + camera 引擎
    ├── comfyui_http/                    ← stdlib HTTP
    └── comfyui_mcp/                     ← stdio JSON-RPC
```

## 输出位置约定

所有运行时写出的文件都落在 `<preset>/temp/` 下，按技能分子目录（见上）。三个 camera CLI 的 `--output-dir` 现在**可选**：不传时默认 `temp/<skill>/`，传了则覆盖；anima 的 `catalog build` / `relation.*` 也有同样的默认路径。清理时删整个 `temp/` 即可，`skills/` 与 `runtime/` 源码保持干净。

## 输出格式：P1 JSON Envelope

每个 CLI 都吐 P1 envelope 到 stdout：

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "command": "author",
  "stage": "t2i",
  "result": { ... },
  "errors": [],
  "advisories": []
}
```

退出码（按 category）：

| Category | Exit |
|---|---|
| `request` | 2 |
| `validation` | 3 |
| `integrity` | 4 |
| `runtime` | 5 |
| `unexpected` | 70 |

> 此表是汇总；**每个 skill 的 SKILL.md 里的 failure-modes 表是权威**（个别 error code 映射到不同 exit，例如 camera-multiview 的 `McpError` 映射到 5、`AssetError` 映射到 4）。

Anima/H3 提示词创作由 prompt-forge 插件的 `prompt_author` / `prompt_compile` / `prompt_audit` 工具承担（不走 CLI）；camera-* CLI 只负责执行渲染，始终吐 envelope。

## 下一步

- **新用户**：先读 [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md)，看任务→工具路由
- **agent**：提示词创作走 prompt-forge 的 14 个工具（`prompt_author` / `prompt_compile` / `prompt_audit` / `prompt_feedback` / `prompt_expand` / `prompt_reverse` / `minimax_scenario` / `style_list` / `style_save` / `profile_list` / `catalog_search` / `catalog_artist_add` / `catalog_relations` / `catalog_build`，逐个的用途与入参见 [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) §1）；渲染执行走 host tool `camera_image` / `camera_video` / `camera_multiview`（loader 已注册）
- **开发者 / 调试**：读 [`docs/development.md`](docs/development.md) + [`docs/cli-cookbook.md`](docs/cli-cookbook.md)
- **已知问题 / 审计**：读 [`docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md`](docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md)

## 参与贡献

欢迎 issue 与 PR：bug 报告请附完整 CLI envelope（`errors[].code`）与 exit code；环境搭建与提交前质量门见 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)（`scripts/check_contracts.py` 契约 gate + `scripts/check_loader.mjs` loader 接线 gate + `plugins/prompt-forge` 测试）。新增动作只改对应 skill 的 `cli.py`——loader 经 `--list-actions` 自动发现；固定工作流 asset 结构不要动（[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) §4）。

Its checked-in file URLs are machine-specific and setup rewrites them, builds the nested plugin and creates a Python environment. Portable built artifacts and a versioned DSH contract remain unverified. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-autorestart

Restart DeepSeek Harness without losing the work that is currently running.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-autorestart?style=flat-square)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-autorestart)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue?style=flat-square)](./LICENSE)
[![dsh-plugin](https://img.shields.io/github/topics/dsh-plugin?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)
[![language](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-JavaScript-yellow?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/Eason-22/dsh-autorestart)

Chinese version: [README.zh.md](docs/README.zh.md)

Current version: **0.9.13**

## What it does

Three small things, all around restarting.

**1. The restart is queued.** An agent asks for a restart; the plugin does not cut off the conversations that are still running. It waits until every one of them is idle, restarts the host, and picks the interrupted work back up — the sessions resume and a goal is re-armed. When several conversations ask at once the requests are merged into one restart, and every requester is woken afterwards. A goal-carrying session cannot block the restart forever: its goal is disarmed before the restart (the running round still finishes) and re-armed after it.

**2. It backs up before each restart.** The configuration and the local `link:` plugin directories are saved under `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-autorestart/backups/`. At most `maxBackups` copies are kept (default 2, range 2–10); old and incomplete ones are pruned. A snapshot that cannot be removed (for example because a file inside it is locked) is reported in `backupHygiene.error` rather than silently kept, so the count can briefly exceed the limit.

**3. It clears the login cookies.** Every launch leaves a `dsh-auth-*` entry behind; they pile up until the request header overflows (~16 KB), the server answers 431, and the client can only say `Web authentication failed`. The plugin clears those stale credentials before each restart and records the outcome in `last-cookie-clear.json`.

There is also a **countdown shutdown**: a moon button at the bottom of the sidebar waits for every conversation to finish, counts down on screen, and powers the machine off.

## What it does not do

- It does **not watch the host** and does **not decide** whether a restart came back.
- It does **not restore anything on its own**. The backup is never applied automatically; it is there for you to inspect or roll back by hand. The one exception is the start-at-login supervisor, if you installed it: that separate process rolls the last snapshot back when the host refuses to start.
- There is **nothing left to run by hand**. If the host will not start, use its own crash dialog or reinstall the plugin.

## Tools for the agent

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `continuum_restart` | Queue a graceful restart (waits for every conversation to be idle) |
| `continuum_status` | Phase, generation, queued requests, which sessions are blocking |
| `continuum_cancel_restart` | Withdraw a queued request (`scope: "mine"` or `"all"`) |
| `continuum_park_goal` | Disarm a goal so a queued restart can proceed |
| `continuum_recover_now` | Retry post-restart recovery immediately |
| `continuum_handoff` | Hand an over-limit session off to a fresh one |
| `continuum_supervisor` | Inspect or install the self-starting supervisor |

## Configuration

The settings page writes these; the defaults are the ones in the code.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `restartMode` | `app` | `app` = ask the desktop client to relaunch itself; `command` = run your own restart command |
| `restartCommand` | `''` | The command used when `restartMode` is `command`; supports the `{pid}`, `{ppid}` and `{app}` placeholders |
| `settleMs` | `2000` | How long the host must stay quiet before the restart may start |
| `restartGraceMs` | `0` | Extra wait after the last conversation went idle, before the host is really restarted — a dropdown: `0` / `5` / `10` / `20` / `30` / `60` seconds. `0` = no extra wait |
| `queuedGraceMs` | `60000` | How long a queued inbox message may sit before it stops blocking the restart. A **running** conversation always blocks |
| `marketStatusUrl` | `''` | Where the plugin market reports whether it is installing something. Empty = the status route of this host (`/dsh-market/status`). Read only — the probe never writes anything |
| `marketProbeTimeoutMs` | `800` | Upper bound of one market probe in milliseconds (a caller can shorten it, never extend it past 800) |
| `marketProbeIntervalMs` | `1500` | How often the market is asked while a restart is waiting (milliseconds) |
| `marketInstallCooldownMs` | `15000` | How long the restart still waits after the market reported that it finished, to bridge the gap between two operations of its queue (milliseconds) |
| `pluginFilesWatch` | `true` | Also wait while the profile's plugin files are being changed — `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `node_modules` and `node_modules-link`. This covers the installs that never go through the market: a manual `pnpm add`, or the host's own plugin manager |
| `pluginFilesStableMs` | `15000` | How long the plugin files must stay unchanged before the change counts as finished (milliseconds) — a dropdown in the settings page: `5` / `10` / `15` / `30` / `60` seconds. A false positive clears itself after this window |
| `pluginFilesMaxBlockMs` | `300000` | The longest a single file-change episode may hold a restart, so a stuck installation cannot pin the host shut (milliseconds) — a dropdown in the settings page: `5` / `10` / `30` / `60` minutes (the shortest wait is 5 minutes) |
| `forceRestartWhenBusy` | `false` | Interrupt a running conversation instead of waiting. The default never interrupts a session |
| `deferPollMs` | `3000` | Poll interval while waiting for the conversations to go idle |
| `relaunchDelaySeconds` | `2` | How long the detached helper waits before it kills the app |
| `restartWindow` | `background` | How the restart command script is started: `background` = no window at all, and it never takes the focus (the default since this version); `foreground` = the visible console window. An existing profile that already says `foreground` keeps it — only a missing or unreadable value falls back to `background` |
| `backupOnRestart` | `true` | Take a copy before every restart. It compares first, so a copy is only written when something changed. Two copies are kept by default and the oldest is deleted when there are more. With the switch off nothing is compared and no copy is taken |
| `backupIncludePlugins` | `true` | The copy holds plugins too, in three kinds: the plugins **you wrote yourself** and online plugins you **downloaded and then changed on this machine** (localised ones) are copied with their files, so a rollback restores them exactly; the rest of the **online third-party plugins, installed as they came**, only get their name and version recorded — their authors keep them up to date, so if something breaks, install them once more (~117 MB here, ~3 s with the files) |
| `maxBackups` | `2` | How many copies to keep (2–10). Its dropdown is a row of its own under **Back up before a restart** — no longer inside the **Backup info** fold. Past that number the oldest copy is deleted; shrinking asks first how many copies will go |
| `restartCommandTimeoutMs` | `30000` | How long the restart command may run before the plugin stops waiting for it |
| `showSleepButton` | `true` | Show the countdown-shutdown button |
| `sleepCountdownSeconds` | `10` | Countdown length before powering off — a dropdown: `0` / `10` / `20` / `30` / `60` seconds. `10` is only the default for an instance that never set it: a profile that already stores `20` (or `30`, or `60`) keeps that value — nothing is migrated or overwritten |
| `sleepCommand` | `''` | Override the power-off command |
| `resumeOnBoot` | `true` | Resume interrupted sessions after a restart |
| `recoveryDelayMs` | `6000` | Wait before the first resume attempt |
| `maxResumeAttempts` | `2` | Resume attempts per session, counted across boots |
| `maxSessions` | `4` | How many sessions are resumed per boot |
| `continuationText` | `''` | Override the continuation prompt text |
| `stateFile` | `''` | Path of the checkpoint file. Empty = `<DSH_HOME>/storages/dsh-autorestart/state.json` |
| `autoReloadPage` | `true` | Reload the web page after a restart |
| `blockManualRestart` | `true` | Refuse an agent that tries to kill or relaunch DSH by hand, and point it at `continuum_restart` instead |
| `healthPath` | `/__dsh_autorestart/health` | Health check route: the boot id, the pid, the phase and the self-check flags |
| `enabled` | `true` | Turns the whole plugin off |
| `watchEnabled` | `true` | The **plugin watch**: after the host settles, compare what the loaded plugins provide with the previous reading and report what is no longer there. A report, not an automatic repair |
| `watchDelayMs` | `8000` | How long the watch waits after boot before it reads |
| `deferSoftMs`, `deferHardMs`, `deferPolicy` | `300000` / `900000` / `auto` | **Deprecated — read but completely ignored.** A pending restart has no deadline |

Four of the keys above — `restartWindow`, `pluginFilesWatch`, `pluginFilesStableMs` and `pluginFilesMaxBlockMs` —
have a control in the settings page, in the **More settings** block. The four `market*` keys are configuration
keys without a settings-page control; the **More settings** subsection below says which is which.

### The settings page

Every section is one row per thing: the title is on the left, the control is on the right, and the explanation
is folded behind **Show details** (`查看说明`) so the page stays readable. A row that is switched off in its own
title is a **sliding switch**, not a checkbox. The control column is wide enough (260 px, dropdowns at least
200 px) that a long choice such as *Background (no window at all, and it never takes the focus; the default)*
is shown in full instead of being squeezed.

A row that only means something while the row above it is on is drawn as that row's **subordinate**: indented
under it, behind a faint vertical line, and greyed out (its control cannot be used) when the parent is off.

| Section | What is in it |
|---|---|
| **Restart settings** | The wait before the restart, **Back up before a restart** with **two subordinate rows** — **Include the installed plugins in the backup** and **Copies kept** — and the **Backup info** fold (read-only) |
| **Shutdown settings** | The countdown of the graceful shutdown |
| **More settings** | A block of its own, **closed by default**: how the restart command script runs, and the plugin-folder watchdog |
| **Start at login** | How "start at login" works on *this* machine, with copyable commands. The plugin never changes your system configuration for you. Not shown on the desktop client — it relaunches itself, so there is nothing to install |
| **Something is wrong** | The diagnostics and a **Report a problem** button that copies them and opens a pre-filled GitHub issue. The diagnostics carry no access token and no secrets |

**Back up before a restart** compares first, so it says what actually happens: your DSH settings and the plugins
covered by the two rows below it are compared; only when something changed is a new copy written, and when
nothing changed the most recent copy is reused. **Two copies are kept by default** and the oldest is deleted
when there are more — that number is changed under **Copies kept**, the third row of this group. With the
switch off nothing is compared and no copy is taken. A copy is **never restored by itself**: to roll back, press
the button in **Backup info**.

**Include the installed plugins in the backup** splits the plugins into three kinds:

- the plugins **you wrote yourself**, and the online plugins you **downloaded and then changed on this machine**
  (localised ones) — their files are copied, so a rollback restores them exactly as they were;
- the rest of the **online third-party plugins, installed as they came** — only their names and versions are
  recorded and no files are copied; their authors keep them up to date, so if something breaks, install them
  once more.

That split is not a figure of speech: `lib/backup.js` really does treat a hand-written `link`, a localised
`localized` and the remaining `thirdParty` separately, and the localised ones are copied with their files.

**Backup info** is the fold that shows what has been backed up: how many copies there are and what they take
on disk, when a copy is taken, the list with a button that rolls back to that one copy, and the path with a
copy button. Since this version it holds **read-only content only** — the **Copies kept** dropdown moved out of
it and became the third subordinate row of **Back up before a restart**, where the number is actually set. It is
**closed by default** — except on a boot the system had to restore, where it opens itself and says so on its
title, because an intervention is the one thing that must not be hidden.

The **last restart** row is gone from the page: which launcher really ran (`wscript`, the PowerShell fallback,
the foreground window) is still reported by the host — it is in the status payload and in the diagnostics — it
simply does not take up room on the settings page any more.

### More settings (「更多设置」)

A block of its own, after **Shutdown settings** and before **Something is wrong**, **closed by default** —
until you click the title you only see the title.

| Row (as it reads on the page) | Key | Control |
|---|---|---|
| **How the restart command script runs** | `restartWindow` | Dropdown: *Foreground (a window appears briefly)* / *Background (no window at all, and it never takes the focus; the default)* |
| **Do not restart or shut down while plugins are installing** | `pluginFilesWatch` | Sliding switch |
| **How many seconds without a file change mean the plugin is installed** | `pluginFilesStableMs` | Dropdown: 5 / 10 / 15 / 30 / 60 seconds |
| **How long to wait at most for the plugin install** | `pluginFilesMaxBlockMs` | Dropdown: 5 / 10 / 30 / 60 minutes |

The last two are **subordinate to the switch above them**: they are drawn indented under it, and they are
greyed out (their dropdown cannot be used) while that switch is off. Their own sentence says so as well —
"When the switch above is off, these two do nothing."

A value that is not one of the offered choices is not rewritten: it shows up in the dropdown as **Current
value**, so an existing profile keeps working and nothing changes until you pick a choice.

**Background is the default since this version.** The restart command script used to run in the foreground, in
a console window that stayed visible for the length of the grace delay. An existing profile that already says
`foreground` keeps the foreground — the default only fills in a missing or unreadable value. Nothing else about
the restart changed: the wait, the idle gate, the kill of the whole process tree, the cookie clear and the
relaunch happen in the same order. If this machine does not allow such little scripts to run, a hidden
PowerShell runs the same command instead and the reason is written into the restart report.

The four **market probe** keys — `marketStatusUrl`, `marketProbeTimeoutMs`, `marketProbeIntervalMs` and
`marketInstallCooldownMs` — have **no control in the settings page**. They are configuration keys: set them
in the profile row or through the configuration API. The defaults in the table above are the ones the probe
actually uses.

## What the restart waits for

A restart is queued, not cut through. The gate waits for the work that is still going on — and the graceful
shutdown (the moon button) waits for the same three things plus one more, because a shutdown cuts an
installation in half even more surely than a restart does.

| It waits for | How it is decided | What you see |
|---|---|---|
| **Every conversation to be idle** | The plugin asks the host which sessions are still running. A queued (unclaimed) inbox message blocks for at most `queuedGraceMs`; a **running** conversation always blocks | The restart stays queued; `continuum_status` names the sessions that block it |
| **The plugin market to be done** | A read-only `GET` of the market's status route (`/dsh-market/status`): `busy` or `active` means "installing". An answer that cannot be read — a timeout, a 404, a non-2xx answer, a body that is not an object — means **"nothing is being installed"**, and the restart goes on exactly as it did before this feature existed | The restart capsule shows a pill ("waiting for the plugin market to finish installing"); the sidebar dot's tooltip says the same thing |
| **The plugin files to settle** | The profile's `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `node_modules` and `node_modules-link` are fingerprinted; while the fingerprint keeps moving, the restart waits. This catches the installs that never go through the market: a manual `pnpm add`, or the host's own plugin manager | The restart capsule shows a pill ("waiting for a plugin install to finish") |
| **A goal that is still going** (the shutdown only) | A goal counts as running while it is still **armed**, has not reached a terminal phase (`paused` / `blocked` / `complete` / `completed` / `done`) and still has rounds left. A paused goal, a disarmed goal and a finished goal never hold the machine | The shutdown is held and names the goal that is still working |

Both of the installation waits have an upper bound, so a broken signal cannot hold the host for ever:

- **The market**: an "installing" answer is remembered for at most `marketInstallCooldownMs` (15 s by default),
  and only while the market cannot be reached at all. Past that window the market counts as idle.
- **The plugin files**: one episode of file changes holds a restart for at most `pluginFilesMaxBlockMs`
  (5 minutes by default), and it only counts as "changing" while the last change is younger than
  `pluginFilesStableMs` (15 s by default).

Both probes are read-only: one `GET`, no body, no retry, nothing is written.

## Where it writes

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-autorestart/state.json` | Boot generation, phase, per-session restart state |
| `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-autorestart/backups/<stamp>/` | `config/` + `node_modules-link/` of one snapshot |
| `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-autorestart/last-cookie-clear.json` | How many credentials the last clear removed |
| `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-autorestart/access.json` | The loopback port and token the plugin listens on |
| `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-autorestart/last-sleep.json` | When and why the last shutdown intent was cleared (`at` / `reason` / `armedAt` / `countdownSeconds`) |

## About that backup

It holds the **configuration files** (`package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`) and the **plugins that are copied with their files** — the ones you wrote yourself and the online ones you changed on this machine. The **online third-party plugins installed as they came are not in it**: the manifest only records their name and version, and they can be reinstalled from `package.json` + `pnpm-lock.yaml`. So it is good for "what did this look like before" and "put this one plugin version back", not a one-click reinstall.

### How big is a backup, and where does the size come from?

**Almost all of it is the plugins that are copied with their files.** The online third-party plugins only
contribute a name and a version to the manifest, so they cost nothing on disk.

Measured on this machine (2026-11-11, desktop client; read from the manifest and the disk):

| Backup | Size | Files | `links` | `localized` | `thirdParty` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2026-11-11T06-36-48-336Z` | **132.1 MB** | **820** | 7 | 0 | 145 (name + version only) |
| `2026-11-11T04-13-04-262Z` | 129.2 MB | 820 | 7 | 0 | 145 (name + version only) |

`linkBytes` is **138,395,369** — essentially every byte of the copy. The two backups have the **same structure**;
only the byte count moved.

Where those 138 MB sit — the seven copied plugins:

| Plugin | Size |
|---|---|
| `dsh-codekg` | **118.7 MB** |
| `dsh-goal-guard` | 6.1 MB |
| `dsh-autorestart` | 5.1 MB |
| `dsh-secret-vault` | 1.2 MB |
| `dsh-github-guard` | 0.4 MB |
| `dsh-security-scan` | 0.3 MB |
| `dsh-web-fetch-fallback` | 0.1 MB |

**`dsh-codekg` alone is about 86% of the whole backup**, and almost all of that is its own `data/` directory
(**114.0 MB**): `snapshots/` **99.6 MB** (108 files, mostly the `run-*.json` baselines the tool writes),
`graphs/` 11.4 MB, `runs/` 2.9 MB. That is **run data the tool produced**, and it grows and shrinks with use and
with the tool's own retention.

So **the size of a backup floats — that is normal.** It does not mean the backup went wrong, and it does not mean
a plugin was left out: the size follows the plugins' own working data. **The things to look at are the file count
and the plugin list**, not the byte total.

**Two kinds of thing are left out of the copy (0.9.9, 2026-11-21).** Both are things that can be rebuilt or that are
scratch space — nothing a restored installation needs in order to RUN:

| Left out | Why | Measured here |
|---|---|---|
| `.git` | rebuildable (clone/fetch) | 56.8 MB / 2,955 files (12 plugins) |
| `.tmp*` work directories | scratch space by construction | 7.3 MB / 358 files |

**Everything else is copied file by file** — the configuration, the plugin sources, **and the plugins' own
dependencies and running data** (`node_modules`, `data/`). Measured on this machine, a copy is **928.1 MB /
35,187 files**, of which 558.5 MB is `dsh-agent-teams`'s dependencies and 317.0 MB is `dsh-codekg`'s graphs.

**Why the dependencies and the data are IN the copy** (user decision, 2026-11-21): an earlier draft of this version
also excluded them, which brought one copy down to 50.9 MB — but then a restore needs a `pnpm install` before a
plugin runs, and `dsh-codekg` has to rebuild its graphs on first use. The user rejected that trade the moment the
price was stated: **a backup has to come back USABLE, not merely small.** So the size is the price of a copy that
runs as-is.

**The manifest records what was skipped** (`skipped: [{ plugin, name, files, bytes }]`), so the two exclusions are
visible rather than implied.

## Platforms

| Platform | Status |
|---|---|
| Windows desktop client (`restartMode: app`) | Verified on the real machine |
| Hosted `dsh web` on WSL with systemd (`restartMode: command`) | Verified on a real instance |
| Hosted `dsh web` on Windows | Not verified |
| WSL without systemd, native Linux | Not verified |

macOS, a remote SSH session without a graphical session and containers are **out of scope** — not
tested, and not supported. The per-capability matrix is in
[docs/platform-matrix.md](docs/platform-matrix.md).

### The floating overlay in hosted `dsh web` — read this before expecting it

The restart / sleep / plugin-failure surfaces are drawn in the **client** slot `shell.overlay` —
"a frame-wide floating layer, above every column and outside their scroll containers". Both facts
below were checked against the shipped packages and a live client, not assumed:

* The slot is declared by the shared workspace UI package
  (`dsh-client-ui-workspace/lib/types/client/contract/slots.d.ts`), which is what the hosted web UI
  mounts — so the slot itself is **not** desktop-only.
* On the desktop client all three of our entries are registered and `active: true`:
  `autorestart-plugin-failure` (order 9), `autorestart-restart-overlay` (order 55),
  `autorestart-sleep-overlay` (order 60). Verified through the live client Slot inspection.

**On hosted web the restart has fewer phases, and one of them does not exist at all.** Measured on
a real instance (0.9.5, `restartMode: command`), sampling `/health?state=1` every 300 ms across a
full restart — 121 frames:

```
waiting      17 frames (~4 s)
DOWN         1 frame          old process gone
restarting    1 frame
DOWN         4 frames         process swap
back          1 frame
DOWN         3 frames
```

**There is no `snapshotting` frame.** On the desktop the backup happens in the old process before it
quits, and that is what the overlay reports. Hosted web does it the other way round: the old process
only goes `waiting → restarting`, and the backup is written by the **new** process at boot, surfaced
as `firstInstallBackup`. So the "backing up, plugins included" sentence has **no phase to attach
to** on the web — it is not hidden, it does not happen there.

The backup itself is still real and still includes plugins on web — verified on the same run:

```
manifest.json  stamp: 2026-11-09T09-41-41-335Z  atLocal: 2026-11-09T17:41:41+08:00
               includePlugins: true   profileDir: /home/fg/.dsh/profiles/web
```

**Treat the restart overlay as a desktop-client feature** and do not plan around seeing it in a
browser. This is a property of "the page is not the host", not a defect fixable from the plugin
side. The restart stays fully visible in the HTTP surface on both platforms —
`GET /__dsh_autorestart/health?state=1` reports the live `restartPhase` and the finished
`firstInstallBackup` — so a scripted check observes what a browser tab cannot.

## Install

From npm:

```
dsh plugin install dsh-autorestart
```

From source:

```
git clone https://github.com/Eason-22/dsh-autorestart.git
cd dsh-autorestart
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/to/dsh-autorestart
```

Inside DSH the equivalent is the `plugin_manager` tool:

```
plugin_manager install_bundle  target = <absolute path to the package>
```

The plugin needs no configuration to work: the defaults queue restarts, take a snapshot before each
one, and clear the stale cookies.

## Uninstall

Remove the `dsh-autorestart` row from your profile's bundle list — in the Plugin Manager of the UI,
or with the `dsh plugin` CLI:

```
dsh plugin remove dsh-autorestart
```

The snapshots under `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-autorestart/backups/` are yours; they are not deleted for you.

## Tests

The plugin ships its own test suite in `plugins/dsh-autorestart/test/`. There is no `node` on `PATH` in the
desktop environment, so the repository ships a script that runs the suite with the bundled Node:

```
pwsh -NoProfile -File plugins/dsh-autorestart/scripts/run-tests.ps1
```

On Windows PowerShell the same thing is:

```
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File plugins/dsh-autorestart/scripts/run-tests.ps1
```

**Do not hand a directory to `node --test`.** Node 24 and newer treat the positional arguments of `--test` as
glob patterns, so `node --test plugins/dsh-autorestart/test` fails with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. The script passes
the glob `plugins/dsh-autorestart/test/*.test.mjs` instead.

All **1250** test cases pass (1250 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped) — measured on 2026-11-18 with the bundled
Node: `tests 1250 / pass 1250 / fail 0`, exit code 0.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# 沙币（shabi-plugin）

> 带眼睛、长期记忆、人格、自主循环、AI 自拍、B 站/小说内容源与 QQ 官方机器人的 DSH 插件。

沙币运行在 [DSH（DeepSeek Harness）](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh) 的 Cordis 插件体系中。所有业务能力都通过统一的 `host` 能力总线访问宿主；缺少截屏、视觉或媒体能力时会降级，不会让宿主崩溃。

## 功能

| 模块 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| 眼睛 | 定时截屏、OCR、视觉理解，输出 `{app, window, text, scene, elements, timestamp}`；宿主没有 `screen.capture` 时自动探测 Linux/macOS/Windows 本机截屏，OCR 自动探测 Tesseract；支持暂停、窗口白名单、敏感区域模糊、失败退避。 |
| 视频完整看 | 0–2 分钟视频逐帧/关键帧/混合抽帧，FFmpeg 解码，逐帧视觉理解，ASR/字幕，1 秒级时间轴，场景/事件，覆盖率 ≥99.9%，断点续看。 |
| 知识 | 从时间轴、画面文字抽取概念/步骤/事实/观点/数据/示例；向量去重、冲突标记、置信度评分、跨视频验证、知识图谱。 |
| 长期记忆 | IOSHB1 分卷、AES-256-GCM、遗忘曲线、归档/压缩/“突然记起来”、INI 导出。 |
| 人格 | 内置傲娇/温柔/毒舌/冷静/元气，支持自定义；人格不能覆盖安全硬约束。 |
| 自主循环 | 感知 → 记忆 → 决策 → 白名单动作 → 审计 → 冷却；每日/每小时上限、安静时段、二次确认。 |
| 兴趣选片 | 观看/收藏/聊天/知识构建偏好，兴趣 + 新鲜度 + 多样性 + epsilon-greedy/UCB。 |
| 内容源 | 用户本人 Cookie 下刷 B 站推荐、按 BV 号学字幕/简介、打开并翻页阅读小说；遇 403/412/风控立即停止。 |
| 桌面协助 | 解释当前屏幕、提醒待办、引用记忆、知识回馈。 |
| AI 自拍 | OpenAI 兼容 / 通用 JSON / SD WebUI，4 张人物参考图，失败固定“拍糊了，等会儿再拍。”，成功标注“（AI 生成）”。 |
| QQ 官方机器人 | Webhook（Ed25519 验签）/ WebSocket，@ 消息去重、限频、复用记忆与人格；不实现个人号自动化。 |
| 安全 | 文件/应用白名单、危险动作二次确认、动作审计、备份回滚、日志脱敏、记忆加密。 |

## 安装

### 从 GitHub 安装（仓库发布后）

```bash
# 先安装官方 DSH CLI
npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh

# 添加插件（把 <profile> 换成你的 profile 名称，如 web / tui）
dsh plugin --profile web add github:ETQWFD/shabi-plugin

# 验证组合包层
dsh --profile <profile> --dump-config
```

安装后应能在 `--dump-config` 中看到类似：

```yaml
# == shabi-plugin
- id: shabi
  name: shabi-plugin
```

> 如果宿主提示“这个包没有声明组合包”，请确认 `package.json` 中有 `dsh.bundle.patch`，且 `engines.dsh` 为 `>=0.2.0`。本仓库已经声明；git 安装不会执行 `prepare`，项目保持纯 JS/ESM。

### 在 DSH Web 中打开设置

安装并启动 `web` profile 后，有两种入口：

1. **DSH 设置页**：左下角账号菜单 → **Settings** → 左侧 **沙币**。
2. **页面右下角悬浮按钮**：**沙币设置**；或直接访问 `http://127.0.0.1:<端口>/shabi/settings`。

设置页会加载完整 schema（眼睛、视频、B 站/小说/学习、自主、人格、自拍、记忆、安全、隐私、QQ、账号、模型、高级）。POST 保存走 `/shabi/api/settings`，立即生效；`dataDir` 修改需重启。

### 从本地目录安装（开发/未发布时）

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add /绝对路径/shabi-plugin
dsh --profile <profile> --dump-config
```

### 独立设置页（无 DSH 时）

```bash
cd shabi-plugin
npm start
# 打开 http://127.0.0.1:3579/shabi/settings
```

独立模式只用于查看/保存配置、测试 API；截屏、LLM、知识抽取等完整能力在 DSH Web profile 中启用。`web` profile 的真实路由和设置 section 已在 DSH `0.2.2-rc.5` 验证。

## 依赖与权限

- Node.js **>=22**（使用全局 `fetch`、`WebSocket`）。
- `ffmpeg` / `ffprobe` 在 `PATH` 中，或在设置里填写绝对路径。
- 可选：Tesseract（OCR）、Whisper/faster-whisper（ASR）。没有时自动降级；Linux 眼睛还需要 grim/scrot/ImageMagick 或 X11（任一即可），macOS 需屏幕录制权限。
- 插件**没有 npm 运行时依赖**，不需要 `npm install`。

权限边界：

1. **截屏**：默认不落盘，只处理内存中的临时图；可暂停、限定窗口、模糊敏感区域。
2. **文件**：只允许插件目录、插件 `dataDir` 和设置中的 `safety.allowedDirs`；记忆库、索引、主密钥、secrets、`.git`、`package.json`、`main.js` 等受保护文件禁止写入/删除。
3. **鼠标键盘**：只允许 `safety.appAllowlist` 中的应用或沙币窗口；高风险输入必须二次确认。
4. **网络**：只访问用户配置的 LLM/图片 API/QQ 官方 API；不内置遥测。
5. **账号**：由用户本人登录并授权；插件不代登录、不保存密码、不读取未授权会话。

## 账号授权

在设置页“账号授权”中，逐平台点击“检查会话”：

- 检查是**只读**的，只调用宿主 `accounts.check`，不会打开网页、不会发消息。
- `authorized=false` 时，视频观看/兴趣选片不会操作该平台。
- 遇到验证码、风控提示、平台限制或规则不允许时，立即停止并提示用户；插件不实现反检测、不绕过限制。
- 不批量私信、不评论骚扰、不刷量；自主行为有频率上限和安静时段。

## 配置

- `config/default.json`：默认配置（会被 `settings.json` 覆盖）。
- 默认数据目录：`~/.dsh/shabi`（不再写进插件安装目录，升级不会丢）。
- `settings.json`：设置页保存的非密钥配置（首次保存后生成）。
- `secrets.ioshb`：`llm.apiKey`、`imageApi.apiKey`、`qqBot.appSecret`、`qqBot.token` 的加密存储。
- `master.key`：AES-256-GCM 主密钥（0600）。优先级：`SHABI_MASTER_KEY` → 本地 `master.key`。
- 环境变量（可选）：
  - `SHABI_LLM_ENDPOINT` / `SHABI_LLM_API_KEY` / `SHABI_LLM_MODEL`
  - `SHABI_IMAGE_ENDPOINT` / `SHABI_IMAGE_API_KEY`
  - `SHABI_CAPTURE_COMMAND` / `SHABI_ASR_COMMAND`
  - `SHABI_MASTER_KEY`（32 字节 base64/hex）

设置页覆盖：眼睛测试/截屏频率/范围、隐私、视频抽帧/覆盖率/分块、B 站 Cookie/推荐条数/无字幕下载、小说默认地址/Cookie、学习笔记上限、自主开关/频率/上限/冷却、人格、图片 API + 测试、记忆管理、安全白名单、QQ 机器人、账号状态、模型、日志。

## 数据格式 IOSHB1

```
偏移  长度  内容
0     6     "IOSHB1"
6     1     version (1)
7     1     flags (1=deflateRaw)
8     4     rawLength (uint32 BE)
12    4     payloadLength (uint32 BE)
16    4     crc32 (uint32 BE, 未压缩 JSON)
20    ...   deflateRaw(JSON)
```

写入：临时文件 → `fsync` → 旧文件 `.bak` → `rename` 原子替换。读取校验 magic/长度/CRC；损坏时回退 `.bak`。记忆内容字段在写入前用 AES-256-GCM 加密，密文前缀 `enc:v1:`。

## 命令

桌面聊天中可用：

- `帮助`
- `看屏幕`
- `发自拍`
- `记住 <内容>` / `忘掉 <关键词>` / `你记得什么`
- `分析视频 <路径或URL>`
- `切换人格 <名称>`
- `开始自主` / `停止自主`
- `状态`

DSH Agent 工具：`shabi_screen`、`shabi_memory_search`、`shabi_memory_write`、`shabi_selfie`、`shabi_video_analyze`、`shabi_video_status`、`shabi_personality`、`shabi_goal`、`shabi_status`。

## 测试与自检

```bash
npm test                 # node:test，单元/集成测试
node main.js selfcheck   # 不需要宿主：配置、IOSHB、记忆、人格、安全、ffmpeg
node main.js video /path/to/video.mp4 hybrid
```

测试覆盖：IOSHB 往返/CRC/备份恢复、记忆写读/遗忘/归档/唤醒/压缩/INI/删除不复活、人格与硬约束、安全路径/确认 token/回滚、知识抽取/证据/去重、真实 FFmpeg 视频覆盖率/每秒 segment/断点、图片 API 成功/失败/AI 标注、QQ 验签/去重/限频、自主循环冷却/限额、兴趣反馈/风控停止、眼睛隐私/降级。

当前验证记录（2026-11-22）：

- `npm test`：**25/25 通过**（含真实 FFmpeg 4 秒视频流水线、知识证据/去重、图片成功与失败降级、QQ Ed25519 验签/去重/限频、自主确认/拒绝、兴趣风控停止、眼睛视觉归一化）。
- 真实 DSH `0.2.2-rc.5`：`dsh plugin --profile headless add <本插件>` 成功，`--dump-config` 出现 `# == shabi-plugin / id: shabi` 层。
- 真实 DSH headless 启动：日志出现“沙币插件已启动”，退出时“沙币插件已卸载”；仅因使用 dummy `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` 触发模型 401，不是插件错误。
- GitHub：<https://github.com/ETQWFD/shabi-plugin>，默认分支 `main`。
- GitHub 直装：全新 profile 执行 `dsh plugin --profile githubtest add github:ETQWFD/shabi-plugin` 成功，`--dump-config` 出现 shabi 层；headless 从 GitHub 源启动正常，9 个 Agent 工具注册无错误。


## 目录

```
shabi-plugin/
├── manifest.json
├── main.js
├── package.json
├── cordis.patch.yml
├── config/
│   ├── default.json
│   ├── personality.json
│   └── settings.schema.json
├── core/
│   ├── content.js          # B 站推荐/字幕学习 + 小说阅读
│   ├── eye.js              # 眼睛
│   ├── videoAnalyzer.js    # 视频完整看
│   ├── knowledge.js        # 知识抽取/图谱
│   ├── memory.js           # 长期记忆
│   ├── personality.js      # 人格
│   ├── autonomy.js         # 自主循环
│   ├── decision.js         # 规则+LLM 决策
│   ├── imageApi.js         # AI 自拍
│   ├── qqBot.js            # QQ 官方机器人
│   ├── safety.js           # 安全护栏
│   └── interest.js         # 兴趣选片
├── lib/                    # 宿主适配/配置/IOSHB/日志/加密/工具
│   └── client.js           # DSH Web settings.section 客户端入口
├── ui/                     # 设置页与聊天增强
├── scripts/                # selfcheck / dev-server
├── tests/                  # node:test
├── docs/                   # 架构、安全、验收
├── memory/                 # 运行时生成（.gitkeep 占位）
├── logs/                   # 运行时生成（.gitkeep 占位）
└── README.md
```

运行时还会生成 `frames/`、`video/`、`selfies/`、`backups/`、`knowledge/`、`settings.json`、`secrets.ioshb`、`master.key`、各类 `*.ioshb`。这些都在 `.gitignore` 中，不会提交。

## 合规说明

- 仅使用 **QQ 官方机器人平台**（Webhook/WebSocket）；不接入个人号，不实现个人号自动化。
- 账号由用户本人登录并授权；插件不代登录、不保存密码。
- 不骚扰其他用户，不批量私信、评论、刷量；自主行为频率接近正常用户，有每日/每小时上限、随机抖动、安静时段。
- 遇到验证码、风控提示、平台限制或规则不允许时立即停止并提示用户；**不实现反检测、不绕过平台限制**。
- AI 自拍一律标注“AI 生成”，不冒充真人；参考图必须由用户提供且有权使用。
- 屏幕、记忆、聊天默认本地处理；日志脱敏；记忆内容加密。

## 已知限制

- DSH Web 设置 section 依赖 `dsh-client-ui-settings`；TUI/headless 使用独立设置页或 `npm start`。
- B 站个性化推荐和字幕需要用户自己的 Cookie；没有 Cookie 时退回公开排行榜，仍可刷到视频，但字幕/高清下载可能不可用。
- 小说抓取只处理静态 HTML 页面；动态渲染、登录墙或强风控站点会返回明确错误，插件不会绕过。
- QQ 图片回复需要 `qqBot.publicBaseUrl` 提供公网可访问 URL；没有公网时只回文字。
- 视频分析使用本机 FFmpeg；长视频受 `video.maxVideoSeconds`（默认 120 秒）限制，这是规格要求。

## 验证记录（1.1.0）

- `npm test`：**31/31 通过**，新增设置路由、B 站推荐、无字幕兜底学习、小说抓取/翻页、学习写记忆测试。
- 真实 DSH `0.2.2-rc.5` Web profile：`dsh plugin --profile web add <本地路径>` 成功；`--dump-config` 出现 `# == shabi-plugin / id: shabi`。
- 真实 Web 启动：`工具注册完成 registered:10 total:10 failures:[]`；不再出现 `cannot create effect on inactive context`。
- 真实 `GET /shabi/settings` 返回 200；设置页渲染 15 个分组，含“B站 / 小说 / 学习”全部字段；`GET /shabi/ui/settings.js` 返回正确 JS（非 Buffer JSON）。
- 真实 `POST /shabi/api/settings` 保存成功；`POST /shabi/api/content {"action":"next"}` 返回真实 B 站视频。
- 真实眼睛：Linux 无宿主 `screen.capture` 时自动用本机截屏，捕获到 `about:blank - Chromium` 窗口，`failures:0`；Tesseract 自动探测可用。

Vision, QQ integration, local memory and autonomous activity expand the capability surface. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-tdx-tools

DeepSeek Harness 插件：将通达信 MCP 行情服务注册为原生工具，提供**实时行情、K 线、期权链**三类数据能力。

---

## 特点

- **常驻会话**：整个 DSH 进程共用一条 MCP 会话，不必每次调用重新握手
- **会话自愈**：检测到服务端回收会话时自动重建并重放，无需人工干预
- **并发安全**：多个工具同时调用互不干扰，共享同一次握手
- **失败即报错**：区分未配置 / 配额不足 / 会话失效 / 超时，给出可操作建议
- **即插即用**：复用宿主 Node 运行时，无需额外依赖

---

## 安装

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Fahaoxi/dsh-tdx-tools
```

安装后需**重启 dsh web**。工具注册发生在插件加载阶段，已建立的会话不会自动获得新工具。

要求 Node.js ≥ 18。

---

## 配置

通过环境变量提供通达信 MCP token：

```powershell
# Windows PowerShell
$env:TDX_MCP_TOKEN = "<your-token>"
```

```sh
# Linux / macOS
export TDX_MCP_TOKEN="<your-token>"
```

`Bearer ` 前缀可省略，插件会自动补全。**token 仅存在于进程内存，不写入磁盘、不输出到日志。**

未配置 token 时，工具返回 `NO_TOKEN` 错误并提示如何配置，不会返回任何替代数据。

---

## 工具

| 工具 | 用途 | 关键参数 |
|---|---|---|
| `tdx_quote` | 实时行情快照，含买卖五档 | `code`、`setcode` |
| `tdx_kline` | 日 / 周 / 月 K 线 | `code`、`period`（`4` = 日线） |
| `tdx_months` | 可交易期权月份及到期日 | `underly` |
| `tdx_chain` | 某月完整期权链：行权价、合约代码、IV、Greeks、到期日 | `month`、`underly` |

### 推荐调用顺序

```
tdx_months  →  tdx_chain(month)  →  tdx_quote(setcode=9) 逐腿获取实际盘口
```

期权链为**两步调用**：先由 `tdx_months` 取得可用月份，再以该月份调用 `tdx_chain`。月份不应推测。

### 使用注意

- **T-quote 的 `NOW` 字段不是盘口价**。需要真实买卖报价时，应对单腿调用 `tdx_quote` 并指定 `setcode=9`。
- **T-quote 返回的 Greeks 与其展示的 IV 不自洽**。如需用于定价或风险计算，应以 BSM 重新计算（无风险利率取 0，T 按日历日 / 365）。

### setcode 对照

| 值 | 市场 |
|---|---|
| `0` | 深圳证券交易所 |
| `1` | 上海证券交易所 |
| `9` | 期权单腿 |
| `31` | 香港交易所 |

---

## 返回字段

每次调用除业务文本外，还包含以下元信息：

| 字段 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `ok` | 是否成功 |
| `tool` | 实际调用的服务端工具名 |
| `version` | 插件版本，便于确认装的是哪一版 |
| `reinitCount` | 累计会话重建次数；`0` 表示会话一直正常 |

### 长响应截断

单次返回超过 24,000 字符时自动截断，并附上原始长度与缩小查询范围的建议。这是为了避免挤占模型上下文，不是数据缺失。

---

## 错误处理

| code | 含义 | 处理 |
|---|---|---|
| `NO_TOKEN` | 未配置 `TDX_MCP_TOKEN` | 设置环境变量后重启 |
| `QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` | 通达信配额不足 | 充值后自动恢复 |
| `SESSION_EXPIRED` | 会话失效且重建失败 | 通常为网络中断，稍后重试 |
| `TIMEOUT` | 请求超时 | 检查网络后重试 |
| `FETCH_FAILED` | 服务端返回其他错误 | 检查 token 是否有效 |

配额不足时服务端返回：

```
TDX MCP quota is below 10. Please recharge before continuing.
leftValue: <remaining>
```

到 <https://vip.tdx.com.cn> 充值即可，无需修改配置。

插件遵循**失败即失败**原则：取数异常时返回明确错误码，不以空值或推测值替代。

---

## 性能

| 场景 | 耗时 |
|---|---|
| 首次调用（含握手） | ~350 ms |
| 后续调用（复用会话） | ~150 ms |
| 10 个并发调用 | ~260 ms，共 1 次握手 |

对比每次新建连接的实现（约 560 ms/次），复用会话约快 3.3 倍。

---

## 兼容性

- 与 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` 可共存，互不干扰
- 不修改任何既有配置行（`cordis.patch.yml` 仅注册自身）
- 包内 `scripts/tdx_fetch.cjs` 保留为独立 CLI，可脱离插件单独使用

---

## 许可

MIT License。

本项目为非官方插件，与通达信官方无隶属或合作关系。使用通达信 MCP 服务需自行申请并遵守其服务条款。

decision.reason: Held for versioned DSH compatibility. The MIT Git-source bundle registers native DSH tools and a persistent external market-data client. Captured declarations do not establish a versioned DSH host contract; external MCP/process and session-recovery behavior remain runtime risks. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.
