evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-sr-ledger **A systematic-review ledger that survives review: append-only, dual-screened, PRISMA 2020, audit-verifiable.** *Records the protocol, every screening decision with reviewer and stage, conflict adjudications and RoB/GRADE assessments — then derives the PRISMA flow and exports the evidence table. Nothing is silently resolved.* Last verified on DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.2.3-alpha.1` (2026-11-22). [简体中文](README-zh.md) · [Español](README-es.md) · [Português](README-pt.md) · [हिन्दी](README-hi.md) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%5E22.19%20%7C%7C%20%3E%3D24.9-brightgreen.svg)]()
--- ## What it does - **`sr_init`** — create/revise the protocol (PICO, include/exclude criteria, per-source identification counts, manual PRISMA boxes) and import records (deduplicated by DOI/PMID/arXiv/title). Every call is a new revision plus an audit event; the full revision is also appended to `review-history.jsonl`, so the criteria a decision was made under remain reconstructable. - **`sr_import`** — import RIS / BibTeX / CSL-JSON / CSV exports (inline content or a `ctx.fs` path). Parsed records go through the same `sr_init` path, so dedupe, revision bump and audit behave identically. Entries without a title are skipped and counted; it never searches or fetches. - **`sr_screen`** — record `include`/`exclude` at `title-abstract` or `full-text`. Two reviewers disagreeing = **conflict**; only an `adjudicator` can settle it, and only when a conflict exists. Exclusions require a reason. RoB 2 / ROBINS-I / GRADE assessments attach to the same ledger. - **`sr_prisma`** — derive the PRISMA 2020 counts, verify the hash-chained audit log, list integrity issues, and write `prisma.json`, `prisma.md`, `evidence-table.md`, `ledger.json` under `/exports`. *Structure: protocol → screening → derivation; `counts` and `integrity` are the two outputs, a conflict stays open until an adjudicator acts, and every protocol revision is hash-chained. The token labels inside the diagram are the real tool names, field names and export files, so the same picture serves all five languages.* ## What it does not do - **No searching or retrieval.** Import records from paper-search / Zotero / PubMed exports. - **No full-text reading.** Screening decisions are human judgements; the ledger records them. - **No meta-analysis.** Effect sizes and pooling belong to `dsh-meta-analysis`. - **No automatic conflict resolution.** A conflict stays open until an adjudicator acts. - **No risk-of-bias automation.** It stores and summarises assessments; it does not infer them from a paper. ## PRISMA boxes | Box | Source | |---|---| | Records identified | `identification` per source (manual; fallback = imported records, labelled in the report) | | Duplicates removed | `manual.duplicatesRemoved` | | Records screened | identified − duplicates | | Excluded at title/abstract | derived from final decisions | | Reports sought for retrieval | final TA includes | | Reports not retrieved | `manual.recordsNotRetrieved` | | Assessed for eligibility | sought − not retrieved | | Excluded at full text (+ reasons) | derived; reasons required | | Studies included | final full-text includes | | Reports of included studies | `manual.reportsOfIncludedStudies` (default = included) | ## Integrity issues (never hidden) `unknown_record`, `exclude_without_reason`, `adjudication_without_conflict`, `duplicate_decision`, `full_text_without_ta_include`, `open_conflicts`, `identification_counts_missing`, `no_records`, `included_without_assessment`, `assessment_of_excluded` — plus audit-chain failures from `sr_prisma.integrity`. Errors make the export honest; warnings are surfaced in the Markdown. ## Tools ### `sr_init` `{ title?, pico?, criteria?, identification?, manual?, records? }` → `{ ok, review, imported: {added, skipped}, recordCount }`. ### `sr_import` `{ content | path, format?, title?, identification?, manual? }`. `format` defaults to detection (`ris` / `bibtex` / `csl-json` / `csv`); `path` needs `ctx.fs`. Returns `{ ok, format, parsed, skipped, imported: { added, skipped }, recordCount, warnings, review }`. A file with no usable title fails as `EMPTY_IMPORT` instead of importing nothing silently. ### `sr_screen` `{ recordId, reviewer, stage, decision, reason?, role?, assessment? }` → `{ ok, state, openConflicts, assessment? }`. ### `sr_prisma` `{}` → `{ ok, counts, issues, robSummary, integrity, exports }`. ### Error codes `INVALID_INPUT` · `NOT_INITIALIZED` · `RECORD_UNKNOWN` · `NO_CONFLICT` · `IO` ## Compatibility & install | | | |---|---| | DeepSeek Harness | **`dsh-v0.2.2-rc.4`** (verified 2026-11-18); peer `>=0.2.2-0 <0.3.0 \|\| >=0.2.2-0 <0.3.0` | | Node | `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.9.0` (tested `24.22.1`), ESM only | | Peers | `@perrylink/dsh-research-core ^0.1.0`, `@deepseek-ai/cordis ^4.0.5-alpha.1`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery ^3.18.5-alpha.1` | | Runtime dependencies | **zero** | ```sh dsh plugin --profile add @perrylink/dsh-research-core dsh-sr-ledger dsh --profile --dump-config | grep dsh-sr-ledger ``` ## Configuration | Key | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `true` | `false` mounts nothing | | `root` | `.sr-ledger` | ledger root (`review.json`, `review-history.jsonl`, journals, `exports/`) | ## Security boundaries - Local only: no network calls, no telemetry. - Append-only journals; every protocol revision is preserved in `review-history.jsonl` before `review.json` is updated. - Audit events are hash-chained with the REP core helpers; `sr_prisma` verifies the chain. - No PII handling beyond reviewer names the user supplies (use identifiers, not personal data). ## Evaluation ![dsh-sr-ledger evaluation: the real verbose run of the ledger spec — 12 cases covering protocol revisions, dual-screening conflicts, adjudication-only resolution, PRISMA derivation and audit-chain tamper detection](docs/assets/dsh-sr-ledger-demo.gif) *Animated: the real `pnpm exec vitest run test/ledger.spec.ts` output on 2026-11-21 — the ledger invariants spec, one of the four spec files in this repository. Pass markers and timings are omitted; the case names and the summary lines are verbatim.* **27 tests**: protocol revision, full revision history and dedupe, invalid-record rejection, dual-screening conflict creation, adjudication-only resolution, exclusion-reason enforcement, adjudication-without-conflict rejection, unknown-record rejection, atomic rejection of an invalid assessment/role, RoB/GRADE recording, PRISMA count derivation, export bundle contents, audit-chain tamper detection, IO mapping, tool schemas and end-to-end execution, package contract. No benchmark is claimed: the ledger is bookkeeping with explicit invariants, not a detector. The invariants are the tests. ## Known limitations (v0.1) - One review per `root`; multiple reviews need multiple profile configs or roots. - `identification` counts are manual; the plugin does not search. - No PRISMA-for-individual-studies variant, no forest plots, no GRADE evidence-profile tables. - Reviewer identity is whatever the caller supplies; there is no authentication. ## License Apache-2.0. No third-party runtime code.

decision.reason: Held for package or companion artifact mapping. Apache-2.0, exact npm gitHead and DSH peers are present. Native TypeScript registers screening and PRISMA tools, but the declared lib/index.js and distributed research-core integration are not mapped to captured executable artifacts. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-statcheck **Recompute the statistics a manuscript reports — and flag the ones that do not add up.** *It is arithmetic, not accusation: each finding shows the reported statistic, the p value it actually implies, and the exact characters it came from.* [简体中文](README-zh.md) · [Español](README-es.md) · [Português](README-pt.md) · [हिन्दी](README-hi.md) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%5E22.19%20%7C%7C%20%3E%3D24.9-brightgreen.svg)]()
--- ## What it does - Parses APA-style reports: `t(df)`, `F(df1, df2)`, `χ²(df)`, `r(df)`, `z`, each with a nearby `p = …`, `p < …` or `p > …` and an optional `95% CI [lo, hi]`. - Recomputes the p value from the reported statistic with zero-dependency distributions (two-tailed t/r/z, upper-tail F/χ²). - Flags self-inconsistency with the reported value, the recomputed value, the character range and a stable issue code. - Checks the CI against significance (a significant p with a CI that includes 0 is a contradiction). - Emits Markdown and **SARIF 2.1.0**, and registers the analyzed text as a REP v1 evidence item whose checks are the findings. *Structure: parse → recompute → judge; `findings[]` and `summary` are the two outputs, and `stat_report` renders them as Markdown and SARIF 2.1.0. The token labels inside the diagram are the real tool, check and issue names, so the same picture serves all five languages.* ## What it does not do - **No data re-analysis.** It cannot know whether the reported statistic is appropriate for the design. - **No misconduct claims.** A finding means “the reported p does not follow from the reported statistic”. It is a candidate for human review, never a verdict about authors. - **No PDF/OCR.** Extract text first (`dsh-doc-anchor`) and pass `text` or a `.txt/.md/.tex/.html` path. - **No model/assumption checks**, no multiple-comparison correction, no sample-size inference. - **No silent tolerance widening.** The rounding rule is fixed and documented; a flagged value stays flagged. ## Compatibility | | | |---|---| | DeepSeek Harness | **`dsh-v0.2.3-alpha.1`** (verified 2026-11-22); peer line `>=0.2.1-0 <0.3.0 \|\| >=0.2.2-0 <0.3.0` | | Node | `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.9.0` (tested on `24.22.1`), ESM only | | Peers | `@perrylink/dsh-research-core ^0.1.0`, `@deepseek-ai/cordis ^4.0.5-alpha.1`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery ^3.18.5-alpha.1` | | Runtime dependencies | **zero** | ```sh dsh plugin --profile add @perrylink/dsh-research-core dsh-statcheck dsh --profile --dump-config | grep dsh-statcheck dsh plugin --profile remove dsh-statcheck ``` ## Tools ### `stat_check` `{ text?, path?, persist?, maxFindings? }` → `{ ok, summary, findings[], source, evidenceId?, recordPath? }`. Each finding: `statistic`, `df`, `text`, `charStart`, `charEnd`, `reported { statistic, p, pKind, pValue, ci? }`, `recomputed { p }`, `status` (`consistent`/`inconsistent`/`unparsed`), `issue?` (`p-value`/`p-threshold`/`ci`/`format`/`df`), `severity`, `detail`. ### `stat_recompute` `{ statistic: 't'|'F'|'chi2'|'r'|'z', value, df[], p? }` → `{ ok, p, judgment? }`. t/r/z are two-tailed; F/χ² upper-tail. `p` uses the same rounding rule as `stat_check`. ### `stat_report` `{ findings, text? }` → `{ ok, markdown, sarif, summary }`. SARIF carries one error result per inconsistent finding. Pass the original manuscript text to map each finding's `charStart` to a real SARIF `startLine`/`startColumn`; without `text`, the region falls back to line 1 plus a character column (the `properties.charStart`/`charEnd` are always exact). ### Error codes `INVALID_INPUT` · `NOT_FOUND` · `PATH_ESCAPE` · `NOT_A_FILE` · `TOO_LARGE` · `OUT_OF_DOMAIN` · `STORE_ERROR` ## The rounding rule (documented, not tuned) A reported `p = x` is consistent when `|recomputed − x| ≤ 0.5 × 10^-decimals + 0.001`. The extra `0.001` absorbs the fact that the statistic itself is often reported rounded (e.g. `t = 2.50` implies p ≈ .01855, commonly written `.019`). `p < X` is consistent when the recomputed value is below `X`; `p > X` when above. ## Configuration | Key | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `true` | `false` mounts nothing | | `root` | `.statcheck` | store + records root | | `workspaceRoot` | `process.cwd()` | manuscript paths must resolve inside it | | `maxChars` | `2000000` | analyzed-character cap (over-limit fails, never truncates) | | `maxFindings` | `500` | findings per call | | `persist` | `true` | store a snapshot + REP record | ## Evaluation ![dsh-statcheck benchmark: a real run over 30 frozen statistics cases — inconsistent precision, recall and F1 are 1, the clean false-positive rate is 0, and exact accuracy is 1](docs/assets/dsh-statcheck-demo.gif) *Animated: the benchmark adapter's real stdout over the 30 frozen statistics cases (`node bench/run-stats.mjs` with `BENCH_DIR` pointing at the frozen `dsh-research-bench` checkout, no network; re-run 2026-11-21). The perfect scores describe these constructed critical-value cases only — the scope warning below still applies.* ### Benchmark — `dsh-research-bench` stats v0.1.0 (30 cases) ```sh pnpm run bench:stats ``` | metric | value | |---|---:| | inconsistent precision | **1.00** | | inconsistent recall | **1.00** | | inconsistent F1 | **1.00** | | clean false-positive rate | **0.00** | | issue accuracy when flagged | **1.00** | | exact accuracy | **1.00** | Raw per-case predictions: [`bench/results-stats.json`](bench/results-stats.json). **Scope warning**: the dataset is small, synthetic and clean (10 consistent + 20 inconsistent sentences around published critical values). A perfect score shows the parser and the recomputation agree with the critical-value labels on these constructions; it does **not** estimate real-manuscript accuracy. The rounding rule and issue codes are documented so a reader can disagree with a specific finding. ### Tests - **43 tests across 6 files**: distribution tails against published critical values (t/F/χ²/r/z), parsing (all families, offsets, thresholds, CIs, multiple statistics, unparsed), judging (p-value, threshold, format, CI, df, negative F/χ² domains), runtime (evidence + valid REP record, re-check without an evidence conflict, findings-cap clamp, file/media type, persist=false, path escapes, size cap), tools (schemas, success/failure, SARIF incl. a null recomputed p and line/column mapping from optional text), package contract. ## Known limitations (v0.1) - One-sided tests, fractional Welch df, multi-model tables and within-text references such as “see Table 2” are not modeled. - Only APA-style inline reports are parsed; `p` values in tables are out of scope. - CI-versus-p checking assumes a two-sided test of the same effect at α = .05. - No correction for multiple comparisons. - SARIF line/column mapping needs the optional `stat_report` `text`; without it the region is line 1 + character column (the exact `charStart`/`charEnd` properties are always present). ## License Apache-2.0. No third-party runtime code.

decision.reason: Held for package or companion artifact mapping. Apache-2.0, exact npm gitHead and DSH peers are present. Source registers native statistical checking/report tools; the declared lib/index.js is missing and the built research-core evidence adapter remains unverified. Findings are for human review, not conclusions about authors. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-test-drive **在一次性 profile 里装、启动、断言、卸载、清理——把「装一下看看能不能跑」变成可复现的流水线。** 面向 DeepSeek Harness 插件的隔离式安装冒烟实测：每个目标独占一个、`mkdtemp` 根（一次性 `DSH_HOME`、一次性工作目录、重定向的 pnpm store），你真实的 `~/.dsh` 从头到尾不被读写，结果落成下游可直接消费的结构化记录。 最近一次核验：DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.2.3-alpha.1`（2026-11-22）。 [安装](#三步上手) · [配置](#配置) · [FAQ](#faq) · [简体中文](README.md) · [English](README.en.md) · [Español](README.es.md) · 社区插件，与 DeepSeek 官方无关。唯一仓库：（Gitee 为镜像）。 ## 它是什么 ![dsh-test-drive 真实终端运行](docs/assets/dsh-test-drive-demo.gif) *本仓库一次真实运行的动图回放。* `dsh-test-drive` 把「这个插件到底装不装得上、启不启得来」变成一条六段流水线：`dsh plugin add` 装进一个一次性 `DSH_HOME` → `--dump-config` 核对 bundle patch 层确实生效 → headless 启动一遍并扫描 loader 失败标记 → 可选地做一次能力断言（让 agent 调用某个具名工具或命令，核对持久会话日志里确实记下了这次调用、观察输出里确实出现期望字面量）→ `dsh plugin remove` → 按 dry-run → 隔离改名 → 删除的阶梯清掉本插件拥有的临时根。每段都带状态、退出码、耗时与脱敏后的输出尾部，最终是一条 `schema: "dsh-test-drive/v1"` 的结构化记录：单目标用 `test_drive`，批量用 `/testdrive`，回看用 `drive_report`。 ## 三步上手 1. **安装**（两通道）： ```sh # npm 渠道（已发布版本；预构建包无需构建许可） dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-test-drive # git 渠道（最新 main；等价于 git+https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-test-drive.git） dsh plugin --profile web add github:PerryLink/dsh-test-drive# ``` git 渠道首次 `add` 会因 pnpm 拦截该包的 `prepare` 构建而失败；把 pnpm 打印的精确键复制进 profile 的 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 后重跑： ```yaml allowBuilds: 'dsh-test-drive': true ``` npm 通道的预构建包不需要构建许可。重启 profile 后，即可在会话中使用 `test_drive` / `/testdrive`。 2. **最小配置**（默认即可用；只有要跑能力断言时才需要 `capability.*` 与 `forwardEnv`）： ```yaml - insert: - id: test-drive name: dsh-test-drive config: headlessTask: "Reply with exactly: ok" forwardEnv: [DEEPSEEK_API_KEY] capability: enabled: true kind: tool name: plugin_vet args: '{}' expect: pass ``` 3. **验证已生效**（重启后）： ```sh dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A3 'id: test-drive' ``` 然后对一个已知目标发起第一次实测： ```text test_drive({ target: "dsh-click" }) → verdict pass · tdr_0b9b6e6a61e3e80cc4620f2e · 完整记录见下方「示例」 ``` **卸载**：`dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-test-drive`（或从 profile patch 删掉该行）。 > `test_drive` 需要一个能启动**第二个** headless DSH 进程的 `dsh` CLI。DSH Desktop 的 launcher（`dsh.CMD`）只允许 `dsh plugin …`、`--dump-config` 与 `--version`，会按策略拒绝第二次 headless 启动——报错会明确说明这一点，而不是「cannot parse npm shim」。请把 `config.dshBin` 指向 npm/pnpm 安装的 `dsh` CLI，或普通 Node + dsh JS 入口。
从 DSH Desktop 市场安装 所有 PerryLink 插件均可在 DSH Desktop 内置市场中浏览：**市场 → 来源 → 添加来源 → 粘贴** `https://perrylink-dsh-catalog.perrylink.workers.dev/catalog-source.json` **→ 选中**。安装仍需通过市场的 npm 身份校验与你的确认。
## 核心能力 `dsh-test-drive` 把一次「装机验证」拆成可观察、可回放的阶段： - **`test_drive` 工具** —— 单个目标跑完整流水线，同步返回结构化记录；传 `background: true` 则启动 `drive-batch` 后台任务并返回 `{ kind: 'background', jobId }`。 - **`/testdrive <目标...>` 命令** —— 空格/逗号分隔的目标列表，作为一个 `drive-batch` 后台任务批量跑；进度经任务输出流式推送，最后产出矩阵报告（JSON + Markdown），末行给出矩阵 id。 - **`drive_report` 工具** —— 按 id 取回任意单次记录（`tdr_...`）、矩阵（`tdm_...`），或不传 id 取最新矩阵，以 Markdown 渲染。 - **能力断言** —— 不止于「启动并退出」：可选的 `capability` 阶段让 agent 以 `args` 调用具名工具（`kind: tool`）或运行 `/命令`（`kind: command`），核对持久会话日志确实记下这次调用、且观察输出包含 `expect`。干净启动只是冒烟，`observed` 才证明具名能力真实可用。 - **结构化结果** —— 每条记录带判别符 `schema: "dsh-test-drive/v1"`，关键字段均为一级字段：`stages.install.status`、`stages.smoke.status`、`stages.capability.status`、各阶段 `durationMs`、脱敏后的 `summary` / `outputTail`，以及总判定 `verdict`（`pass` / `fail` / `partial` / `unknown`）。这是下游评分方（dsh-score）消费的机器可读契约。 - **结构安全** —— 每个临时目录都由本插件以专属前缀 `dsh-test-drive-` 创建、登记在活跃所有权注册表中，且只经 dry-run → 隔离改名 → 删除的阶梯清理。宿主机 profile 永不被读取或写入。 ```text target ──dsh plugin add──▶ 一次性 DSH_HOME ──--dump-config──▶ patch 层 │ │ ├──headless boot──▶ FAILED-marker 扫描 ├──capability────▶ tool/command + 会话日志 └──dsh plugin remove──▶ quarantine → delete ``` ### 工具面 | 表面 | 形态 | 返回 / 说明 | |---|---|---| | `test_drive` | 工具 | 完整结构化记录（同步），或 `{ kind: 'background', jobId }` | | `/testdrive` | 命令 | 一个 `drive-batch` 后台任务；末行给出供 `drive_report` 使用的矩阵 id | | `drive_report` | 工具 | `tdr_...` 单次记录 / `tdm_...` 矩阵 / 最新矩阵，Markdown 渲染 | `test_drive` 的 `target` 接受 git 规格（`github:owner/repo#sha`、`git+https://...`）、npm 包名、本地路径或 `.tgz` 压缩包；`capability` 形如 `{ kind: 'tool' | 'command', name, args, expect }`，需要 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`（宿主环境或 `forwardEnv`），缺失时该阶段为 `skipped`，绝不算失败。 ### 结构化结果 判定规则：安装失败、启动失败（`smoke.fail`）、或能力阶段到达 `not-registered` / `failed` ⇒ `fail`；安装通过 + patch 生效 + 启动干净（`pass` / `boot-ok`）+ 卸载通过 ⇒ `pass`（能力阶段 `observed` 时附说明）；已安装但后续保证缺失 ⇒ `partial`；其余 ⇒ `unknown`。

profile patch 中的覆盖示例： ```yaml - insert: - id: test-drive name: dsh-test-drive config: headlessTask: "Reply with exactly: ok" forwardEnv: [DEEPSEEK_API_KEY] capability: enabled: true kind: tool name: plugin_vet args: '{}' expect: pass ``` ## FAQ
会碰我真实的 ~/.dsh 吗？ 不会。每次实测都在 OS 临时目录下的一个全新 `mkdtemp` 根内进行：一次性 `DSH_HOME`、一次性工作目录、重定向的 pnpm store，被测插件的代码只在那套临时 profile 里执行。宿主机 profile 既不被读取也不被写入，结构化记录里的 `isolation.hostHomeTouched` 恒为 `false`。清理只认本插件登记过的目录，绝不扫描 `%TEMP%`、不碰他人前缀、不碰真实家目录。
组合里没有 storageDomain 时，报告会丢吗？ 工具照常工作，只是报告不持久化：插件会记录一条原因后禁用持久化，`drive_report` 会如实报错而不是假装成功。反过来，有 `storageDomain` 的组合会把记录写进 `test_drive` 领域（表 `runs`、`matrices` 与 latest-matrix 指针）。
被测插件的子进程会拿到我的密钥吗？ 默认不会。子进程继承的是**已剥离凭据**的环境；除非你在 `forwardEnv` 里显式点名某个变量（只写变量**名**），宿主机密钥不会进入被测 profile，而且这些值永不落日志。所有报告与日志字符串还会过纯函数脱敏：令牌字面量、URL 凭据、bearer 头被涂红，临时根路径替换为 ``，输出尾部按字节封顶。
为什么冒烟阶段经常只到 boot-ok？ 因为启动检查本身不需要凭据，而真跑完一句任务需要模型凭据。没有凭据时插件如实上报 `boot-ok`——既没有 loader 失败，也没有跑完任务——而不是把没验证过的东西记成 `pass`。要让它走到 `pass`，请显式配置 `forwardEnv` 转发凭据（值仍不进日志）。
实测失败时临时目录会残留吗？ 不会静默残留。清理在 `finally` 里执行，覆盖成功、失败、超时与中止，插件卸载时还会再扫一次；删除前先把根目录改名为 `dsh-test-drive-quarantine-<时间戳>` 隔离目录再核验，失败时目录保持隔离并如实上报。想保留现场取证就设 `keepTempDirs: true`，此时所有权会被放弃，由你自己清理。
## 安全边界 - **隔离**：每次实测在 OS 临时目录下全新 `mkdtemp` 根内进行：一次性 `DSH_HOME`、一次性工作目录、重定向的 pnpm store。被测插件代码只在那个 profile 中运行；宿主机 profile 不受影响。 - **所有权**：活跃注册表记录本插件实例创建的每个根目录。清理会拒绝任何「非注册的、不在 OS 临时目录直接子级、不携带 `dsh-test-drive-` 前缀」的路径——不扫 `%TEMP%` 全量、不碰他人前缀、不碰真实家目录。 - **清理阶梯**：任何变更前先打印完整 dry-run 计划（绝对路径）。删除先把根目录改名为 `dsh-test-drive-quarantine-<时间戳>` 隔离目录，核验后再删；失败则目录保持隔离并如实上报，绝不静默丢弃。成功、失败、超时、中止的所有路径都在 `finally` 中执行清理，插件卸载时再次清扫。 - **`allowBuilds` 是真实权限**：放行 git 包的 `prepare` 构建意味着在安装时执行该包的代码。放行范围仅限一次性 profile，但仍只测你信任的目标，并固定 commit。 - **headless 冒烟默认无密钥**：启动检查不需要凭据；完成一句任务才需要。要转发凭据请显式配置 `forwardEnv`，且绝不记录其值。 ## 权限与数据 - **服务面**：只消费公开服务 —— `ctx.subprocess`、`ctx.jobs`、`ctx.storageDomain`、`ctx.tools`、`ctx.commands`；其中 `storageDomain` 是可选依赖，缺失时启动与实测都不受影响。 - **权限**：`dshWorkshop` manifest 声明 `fs:read`、`fs:write`、`subprocess:spawn`、`session:append`、`network:inherit`、`native-code:none` —— 写权限只用于自己创建的临时根与报告落盘，`network:inherit` 只是继承宿主（被测目标的 registry/git 安装本来就需要网络）。 - **数据**：报告存于 `test_drive` storage-domain（表 `runs`、`matrices`；latest-matrix 指针）；没有该领域时报告不持久化并记录原因。 - **会话日志**：子进程继承已剥离凭据的环境，`forwardEnv` 只转发变量名；所有报告/日志字符串都经纯函数脱敏 —— 令牌字面量、URL 凭据与 bearer 头被涂红，临时根路径被替换为 ``，输出尾部按字节封顶。 ## 已知限制 - **DSH Desktop 不是受支持的测试宿主。** `test_drive` 需要能启动第二个 headless 进程的 `dsh` CLI，而 `dsh.CMD` launcher 只允许 `dsh plugin …`、`--dump-config` 与 `--version`；请把 `dshBin` 指向 npm/pnpm 安装的 `dsh`。 - 安装 registry/git 目标需要子进程 `dsh`/pnpm 具备网络访问。 - 冒烟任务需要模型凭据才能到 `pass`；没有时如实上报 `boot-ok`。 - 没有 `storageDomain` 的组合不持久化报告（`drive_report` 会诚实报错）。 - `dsh` 必须能在 PATH 上定位（或配置 `dshBin`）；Windows 下自动解析 npm 的 `.cmd`/`.bat` shim，若只解析到 `.ps1` 会要求配置 `dshBin`。 - 批默认串行执行；提高 `batchConcurrency` 只影响 pnpm-store 磁盘争用，不影响正确性。 ## 与其他 DSH 插件的互操作性 `dsh-test-drive` 只暴露两个工具与一个命令，不参与别的插件的接缝： - **命名空间隔离。** 只注册 `test_drive`、`drive_report` 两个工具与 `/testdrive` 一条命令，不占用内置工具或插件已用的裸名。 - **不占客户端与 HTTP 资源。** 本包含无 `client/` 半，不注册客户端 slot、不注册 `webServer` 路由、不装 `agent/pre-step` / `tools/post-execute` 等 waterfall 监听器（`AGENTS.md` 明确记录：本插件当前不注册任何 waterfall 监听器），也不改全局对象。 - **无服务键冲突。** 不提供任何 service key，只消费 `subprocess`、`jobs`、`tools`、`commands` 与可选的 `storageDomain`。 - **patch 层只插自己一行。** 组合包 patch 只 `insert` 自己的 `test-drive` 行，从不覆写内置行的 `config`。 - **注册即 effect。** 工具、命令与领域关闭都在 `ctx.effect` 内注册，停止/热重载只撤销自己注册的东西，临时目录注册表也会在 disposer 里扫尾。 ## 兼容性 | 维度 | 状态 | |---|---| | Harness | DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.2.2-rc.4`（GitHub tag，2026-11-18 已核验：完整门禁链 + profile 安装冒烟）。npm 依赖线 `0.1.2-rc.1` 与 `0.1.7-rc.2`；`engines.dsh`：`>=0.2.1-0 <0.3.0 \|\| >=0.2.2-0 <0.3.0` | | Node | `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.9.0` | | 包管理器 | `pnpm@11.7.0` | | 平台 | Windows / macOS / Linux（纯 host 插件，无 UI 半） | | 外部工具 | PATH 上的 `dsh` CLI（自动探测，可解析 npm shim）、PATH 上的 `pnpm` | ## 生态与质量 - [Gitee 镜像](https://gitee.com/perrylink/dsh-test-drive)（同步镜像，以 GitHub 为准） - [dshfind 插件页](https://dshfind.com/plugins/PerryLink/dsh-test-drive)（安装量与排名） - [OpenSSF Scorecard 报告](https://securityscorecards.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/PerryLink/dsh-test-drive)（由 [.github/workflows/scorecard.yml](.github/workflows/scorecard.yml) 驱动） - [dsh-plugin-doctor 验证报告](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-plugin-doctor#verified-徽章)（由本仓的 [.github/workflows/plugin-doctor.yml](.github/workflows/plugin-doctor.yml) 驱动） - [DSH Market](https://dsh.market/)（已上架） - **1024 商店渠道**：先 `npm i -g dsh1024`，再 `dsh1024 plugin --profile web add dsh-test-drive`（计入 [deepseek1024.com](https://deepseek1024.com) 安装排行） - [生态实测知识库](https://perrylink.github.io/dsh-plugin-guide/)：插件开发指南 · 选型实测数据 · 维护取舍判据 ## 开发 ```sh pnpm install # node ^22.19 || >=24.9 pnpm run typecheck # tsc：src + tests，经本地 harness checkout 解析 @deepseek-ai/* pnpm run typecheck:ci # tsc：对照已发布的宿主类型 pnpm test # vitest pnpm run build # node scripts/prepare.mjs（tsdown bundle + 声明） pnpm run verify:self-contained # 依赖 spec 均来自 registry pnpm run verify:artifacts # 发布文件齐全 + lib/index.js 可 import pnpm run check:readmes # 五语 README 一致性 pnpm pack # 发布 tarball ``` - `typecheck` 经本地 harness checkout 解析 `@deepseek-ai/*`；`typecheck:ci` 对照已发布的宿主类型检查。 - 测试使用真实 `Context`/`Session`/`ToolRuntime`/`LocalJobRegistry`/storage 栈 + 脚本化 subprocess provider。 - 真实 CLI 端到端（需网络 + PATH 上的 `dsh`）：`DSH_TESTDRIVE_E2E=1 pnpm run test:e2e` —— 用真实安装冒烟循环实测本包自身 checkout。 - 发布：`node scripts/release.mjs `（升版本、CHANGELOG 落日期、重跑门禁、commit + tag；不 push）。 ### GitHub Action（action.yml） 仓库内置一个 composite [`action.yml`](action.yml)，可在任意插件仓库里 `uses:` 复用：它在一次性隔离 profile 里驱动目标，并输出 CI 消费的报告对 —— Markdown（PR 评论）与 JUnit XML（测试报告/状态检查）。 ```yaml # .github/workflows/test-drive.yml name: test-drive on: [pull_request, workflow_dispatch] jobs: smoke: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - name: Drive this plugin id: drive uses: PerryLink/dsh-test-drive@v0.2.4 with: target: github:${{ github.repository }}#${{ github.sha }} - name: Publish JUnit uses: EnricoMi/publish-unit-test-result-action@v2 with: files: ${{ steps.drive.outputs.junit }} - name: Comment the report run: cat "${{ steps.drive.outputs.markdown }}" ``` `action.yml` 输入：`target`（必填）、`headless-task`（可选冒烟任务）、`dsh-version`（`dsh` CLI 规格）；输出：`markdown`、`junit`（报告路径）与 `verdict`（`pass`/`fail`/`partial`/`unknown`）。驱动本身无需密钥（install → patch 校验 → 启动冒烟 → 卸载 → 清理）；只有 capability 断言需要 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`，缺省时 `skipped` 而不是失败。 同一对报告也可编程取得：`renderDriveResult` / `renderMatrix`（Markdown）与 `renderDriveJUnitXml` / `renderMatrixJUnitXml`（JUnit）从包根导出，作用于已结算的 `DriveResult` 或 `MatrixRecord`。 配图由 [`scripts/gen-readme-assets.py`](scripts/gen-readme-assets.py) 程序化生成（Python + Pillow），可重复执行：`python scripts/gen-readme-assets.py`。 Topics：`dsh`, `dsh-plugin`, `deepseek-harness`, `deepseek`, `cordis`, `plugin-testing`, `install-smoke`, `compatibility-matrix`, `ci` ## 家族与致谢 本项目是 [PerryLink](https://github.com/PerryLink) 维护的 DeepSeek Harness 插件家族成员（全部 Apache-2.0）。如果这个插件帮到了你，**给个 star** —— 它不解锁任何功能，但会让下一个人更容易找到它。 - evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-zotero-bridge **Read a local Zotero library — and register the item as evidence. Never write to it.** *Local API first, a temporary copy of `zotero.sqlite` second, and one REP evidence item per selected paper. No sync, no write, no cloud, no PDF download.* Host compatibility: DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.2.2-rc.4` (verified 2026-11-18). Last verified on DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.2.3-alpha.1` (2026-11-22). [简体中文](README-zh.md) · [Español](README-es.md) · [Português](README-pt.md) · [हिन्दी](README-hi.md) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%5E22.19%20%7C%7C%20%3E%3D24.9-brightgreen.svg)]() [![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh--plugin-✅-green)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)
--- ## Why read-only Your Zotero library is the only copy of years of work. One bad write can corrupt `zotero.sqlite` or desynchronize the desktop client. This plugin therefore has **no write path at all**: it only performs `GET` against the Local API and `SELECT` against a temporary copy of the database. *Structure: probe → read → register; a normalized `ZoteroItem` and its persistence (`rep` / `file` / `none`) are the two outputs, and there is no third path in which the library gets written. The token labels inside the diagram are the real tool, endpoint and field names, so the same picture serves all five languages.* ## Modes | Mode | When | What happens | |---|---|---| | `local-api` | Zotero is running with **Settings → Advanced → “Allow other applications on this computer to communicate with Zotero”** | Reads `http://127.0.0.1:23119/api/users/0/...` (loopback only) | | `sqlite` | Local API is down and `zotero.sqlite` exists | Copies the database to a temp directory, opens the copy read-only, extracts items, deletes the copy | | `unavailable` | Neither | Returns concrete steps instead of an empty result | ## Tools | Tool | Job | |---|---| | `zotero_status` | Probe the API, find the database, report the active mode and read-only policy | | `zotero_search` | Query the library; returns title, creators, year, DOI, abstract, tags, collections, attachment metadata | | `zotero_item` | Read one item by key, including its attachment children | | `zotero_to_rep` | Capture the item as an immutable JSON snapshot + REP evidence (or `/items/.json`) | `zotero_to_rep` does **not** download PDFs. When you need page-level anchors, run `doc_anchor` on the attachment path — the bridge keeps the path in the metadata so the two plugins can meet. ## Install ```sh dsh plugin --profile add dsh-zotero-bridge dsh --profile --dump-config | grep dsh-zotero-bridge ``` Then: ```text Run zotero_status. ``` If it reports `unavailable`, start Zotero and enable the Local API, or set `dataDir` to the directory that holds `zotero.sqlite`. ## Configuration | Key | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `true` | `false` mounts nothing | | `root` | `.zotero-bridge` | item-record fallback root | | `localApiUrl` | `http://127.0.0.1:23119` | loopback only; any other host fails validation | | `dataDir` | auto-detect | Zotero data directory (or the `zotero.sqlite` file) | | `timeoutMs` | `10000` | per-request deadline | | `maxResults` | `25` | search cap (1–100) | ## What it does not do - **No writes.** No create/update/delete, no notes, no tags, no collections, no trash. - **No sync.** It never talks to `api.zotero.org`. - **No PDF download or parsing.** Attachment metadata only; use `dsh-doc-anchor` for text. - **No Web API keys.** The Local API needs no account or key. - **No silent fallback.** If both modes fail, the tool reports `unavailable` with steps. ## Compatibility | | | |---|---| | Zotero | 7+ (Local API opt-in); sqlite fallback reads Zotero 6/7 schema | | Node | `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.9.0` (sqlite uses `node:sqlite`) | | DeepSeek Harness | peer line `dsh-v0.2.2-rc.4`（2026-11-18）；`>=0.2.1-0 <0.3.0 \|\| >=0.2.2-0 <0.3.0` | | Peers | `@perrylink/dsh-research-core ^0.1.0`, `@deepseek-ai/cordis`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` | | Runtime dependencies | **zero** | ## Development ![dsh-zotero-bridge gates: a real run of pnpm run check:lockfile, pnpm test and pnpm verify:package — 5 test files and 16 tests against a scripted Local API and a temporary sqlite copy, read-only package surface, zero runtime dependencies](docs/assets/dsh-zotero-bridge-demo.gif) *Animated: the real `pnpm run check:lockfile`, `pnpm test` and `pnpm verify:package` output on 2026-11-21 (5 test files, 16 tests, scripted fetch + a temporary sqlite copy — no Zotero, no network). The plugin has no CLI, so its documented gates are the run: the lockfile keeps its two-document form, the four tools and the sqlite fallback are exercised, and the package surface is verified read-only.* ```sh pnpm install pnpm run check:lockfile pnpm typecheck pnpm test # fixture DB + mock Local API; no Zotero required pnpm build pnpm verify:package ``` The lockfile is committed exactly as `pnpm install --lockfile-only` writes it (two documents: pnpm's own package-manager document, then the project document), so a local install does not rewrite it. `pnpm run check:lockfile` fails when the lockfile drifts from `package.json` or loses that form. The sqlite test creates a minimal Zotero-shaped database in a temp directory; the Local API test uses a scripted fetch. Real-library acceptance is manual: run `zotero_status` on a machine with Zotero. ## License Apache-2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

decision.reason: Held for package or companion artifact mapping. Apache-2.0, exact npm gitHead and versioned DSH peers are present. TypeScript registers local API/SQLite and evidence-export tools; declared lib/index.js is absent and the built package/native database mapping remains incomplete. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# OAM for DeepSeek Harness

This personal memory plugin uses the OAM HTTP API to recall cited context for human turns and retain human text after completed turns. Use it only in a DSH profile accessible to the owner of the configured OAM user. It excludes subagents. OAM must already be running and processing operations.

When the DSH schedule service is available, the plugin observes named recurring jobs and retains concise definitions, changes, removals, and the latest acknowledged delivery. It excludes prompts, generated output and one-time tasks. A delivery means the scheduler persisted a message to the session; it does not prove the job completed. The profile is the ownership boundary because the catalog has no owner or maintenance classification. A private file under `DSH_HOME` (default `~/.dsh`) preserves each job's current definition observation and timestamp so unchanged snapshots reuse their idempotency key after restart. The catalog exposes only the latest receipt; intermediate deliveries missed while stopped are not recovered. Failed captures are logged, not queued.

Set `OAM_DSH_URL`, `OAM_DSH_USER_ID` and `OAM_DSH_API_KEY` in the DSH process environment. Use an HTTPS origin or a loopback HTTP origin and a user-scoped key. Install this package in the desired DSH profile using the host's plugin manager and restart or reload that profile. The model can use `memory_search` for explicit recall and `memory_remove` for explicit user removal requests. The server's complete context must fit the plugin's `maxContextTokens` configuration (default 18000); oversized results are omitted, with a warning, rather than truncated. Failed capture is logged and is not queued for retry.

Run `npm test` for local HTTP-boundary tests. A live integration requires a separate completed turn, OAM operation readiness, and cited recall in a fresh DSH session; installation or local tests do not prove that path.

## Memory removal

For an explicit user removal request, call `memory_remove` with exactly one `memory_id` or `insight_id`, for example `{"memory_id":"mem_42"}` or `{"insight_id":"ins_7"}`. Resolve the exact ID from dialogue or `memory_search`, which appends each removable item's exact ID alongside its numbered context reference; citation numbers alone are not removal IDs. Clarify ambiguous targets before calling. The tool always uses the configured user and user-scoped key, requires OAM's `source:delete` grant, and is unavailable to subagents. It sends `DELETE /v1/users/{user_id}/memories/{memory_id}` or `DELETE /v1/users/{user_id}/insights/{insight_id}`. A validated `202` receipt confirms exclusion from serving; the reported cleanup status and operation ID describe separate storage cleanup. Invalid requests, failed requests and invalid receipts surface as tool errors.

Completed turns containing a native `memory_remove` tool call or an invocation of this plugin's removal tool retain the original human text and timestamp with `learning_eligible: false`, including failed attempts. Assistant and tool output remain outside capture; later ordinary turns remain eligible. Candidate and confirmation turns without a removal invocation are not classified by this plugin. It does not infer removal intent from arbitrary natural-language text.

## npm installation

Install the independently published 0.0.2 package in the owner-only DSH profile to use exact memory and Insight removal.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile headless add @rocke-dong/oam-dsh@0.0.2
```

No npm login is required for users installing the public package. Supply the OAM environment variables above, then restart or reload that profile. If an earlier local `@rocke2020/oam-dsh` package is installed, remove that package through the same profile's plugin manager before adding the renamed package. Source and archive checks are separate from verification of the actual published package.

## Release archive installation

Download `rocke-dong-oam-dsh-0.0.2.tgz` and `SHA256SUMS` from the same OAM GitHub Release and run `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS` in that directory. No npm account or registry publication is required. DSH may need network access for its own profile dependencies.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile headless add /absolute/path/rocke-dong-oam-dsh-0.0.2.tgz
```

Select the owner-only profile you intend to use, supply the three environment variables above to that DSH process, and restart the profile. Keep the archive available because the profile's package manager may reference its local path. Use `dsh plugin --profile headless remove @rocke-dong/oam-dsh` to remove it. The package contains the plugin entrypoint and profile patch; it does not include or start OAM.

# Open Agent Memory

**Useful memory for everyday AI agents.**

[English](README.md) | [中文](README_CN.md) | [日本語](README_JA.md)

[Get started](#quick-start) · [Performance](#performance--accuracy) · [Integrations](#connect-your-agent) · [Documentation](docs/indexing-retrieval.md) · [Releases](https://github.com/rocke2020/open-agent-memory/releases)

Open Agent Memory (OAM) is a fully open-source memory engine for AI agents. It remembers useful facts, preferences and experiences across conversations, then retrieves relevant evidence with citations when your agent needs it.

Keep your conversations and documents in your own PostgreSQL database, choose your model providers, and inspect what the agent remembers. OAM supplies the memory; your agent writes the answer.

## Performance & Accuracy

**LongMemEval S (LME-500)** measures answer accuracy across 500 questions. The comparison below pairs accuracy with mean saved context size using Hindsight's published Agent Memory Benchmark (AMB) run. [Hindsight's pinned LME-500 result](https://github.com/vectorize-io/agent-memory-benchmark/blob/7021c59c3497d1dd08d61f12fa4629be983fcfb1/outputs/longmemeval/hindsight/rag/s.json.gz)

| Benchmark | OAM | Published Hindsight | Mean saved context |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **LongMemEval S**, accepted answers | **95.2% (476/500)** | 94.6% (473/500) | **11,373.58** vs 43,124.55 tokens (**73.63% fewer**) |
| **BEAM-10M**, mean rubric credit | **78.23%** | 64.08% | **24,676.88** vs 27,373.25 tokens (**9.85% fewer**) |
| **BEAM-10M**, pass rate (score ≥ 0.5) | **86.0% (172/200)** | 73.5% (147/200) | |

**BEAM-10M tests memory at the 10-million-token scale per conversation.** It covers 200 questions across ten histories and tests event ordering, temporal reasoning and contradiction resolution. OAM gained **14.15 percentage points in mean rubric credit and 25 additional passes**. The full result uses 180 current recalls with a **24,000-token** native context cap and 20 previously saved contexts. [BEAM method and results](docs/benchmarks.md#3-beam-10m)

OAM exceeds the top recorded Hindsight scores on both full datasets using low-cost **MiniMax M3.1 Flash** adaptive for answering and judging. [AMB results manifest](https://github.com/vectorize-io/agent-memory-benchmark/blob/c963dba91dfe6c459f64bb871c5dafb2f3de1bf1/results-manifest.json)

**For a fair comparison, both benchmarks use the same questions, reference answers and scoring rules as the published Hindsight runs.** OAM reuses byte-identical answer and judge prompt templates from the pinned AMB sources. Three BEAM judge calls needed a JSON example in the provider wrapper. The judge text and scoring rule stayed the same. [LongMemEval settings](docs/benchmarks.md#1-latest-longmemeval-s-476500-at-18k) · [BEAM protocol](docs/benchmarks.md#3-beam-10m)

The recorded comparisons measure end-to-end results with different models and memory pipelines. Context counts measure saved text with `o200k_base`. LME-500 averages use 497 OAM contexts and 500 Hindsight contexts. Three OAM cases with disputed reference answers count as incorrect in the 500-question score. [LME-500 token recount](docs/benchmarks.md#comparison-with-the-recorded-hindsight-result)

MiniMax lists USD 0.15 per million uncached input tokens and USD 0.60 per million output tokens. [Official MiniMax pricing](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/pricing/overview#llm)

Scores can vary when answer and judge models are rerun. In a [same-input MiniMax example](docs/benchmarks.md#answer-and-judge-variability), one answer was correct and another was incorrect; this illustrates observed variability, not its frequency.

[Results, model pricing and methodology](docs/benchmarks.md) · [LME per-question evidence](https://github.com/rocke2020/open-agent-memory-benchmark/tree/main/eval_results/lme500-20261117) · [BEAM per-question evidence](https://github.com/rocke2020/open-agent-memory-benchmark/tree/main/eval_results/beam10m-20261119)

## Why OAM?

- **Remember across sessions.** Retain useful preferences, decisions and experiences so your agent can use them in a new conversation.
- **Check the evidence.** Recalled memories link back to original source messages. Browse and remove memory through the Memory Inspector.
- **Search conversations and documents together.** Recall relevant learned memory alongside text, HTML, PDF and image Resources; documents stay separate from learned personal memory.
- **Build a useful personal Profile.** Refresh a stored User Profile manually or on a schedule, or generate a custom Profile for a specific purpose.
- **Own your data and models.** Self-host with PostgreSQL/pgvector, configure your own endpoints, and control the recall context budget.

## Quick Start

You need **Docker with Compose**, **Git**, a generation endpoint that supports text and image inputs, and an OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint. OAM has no default model endpoints or credentials. Model preflight and indexing use your configured providers and may incur charges.

### 1. Prepare your settings

```bash
git clone https://github.com/rocke2020/open-agent-memory.git
cd open-agent-memory
cp deploy/.env.example deploy/.env
```

Edit `deploy/.env`:

- Set `VLM_BASE_URL`, `VLM_API_KEY`, `VLM_MODEL` and `OAM_EMBEDDING_URL`, `OAM_EMBEDDING_KEY`, `OAM_EMBEDDING_MODEL` to your provider settings.
- Set each database password and `OAM_ROOT_API_KEY` to a separate random value; generate each with `openssl rand -hex 24`.
- The default embedding dimension is **1024**. If your endpoint returns a different supported size, set `index.embedding_dimensions` in `deploy/oam.yaml` **before initialization**. See [model configuration](docs/operations.md#1-configuration).

### 2. Start OAM

```bash
docker compose --env-file deploy/.env -f deploy/compose.yaml up -d --wait postgres
docker compose --env-file deploy/.env -f deploy/compose.yaml run migrate
docker compose --env-file deploy/.env -f deploy/compose.yaml exec -T postgres psql -U postgres -d oam -f /bootstrap/runtime-roles.sql
docker compose --env-file deploy/.env -f deploy/compose.yaml run api preflight --json
docker compose --env-file deploy/.env -f deploy/compose.yaml up -d --wait api worker
```

Stop if a command fails and resolve the reported error before continuing. The Compose file selects the **v0.2.0** image for Linux AMD64 or ARM64. See the [deployment guide](deploy/README.md) for ports, model servers on your host, source builds and replica setup.

### 3. Store and recall your first memory

Open the **Memory Inspector at <http://127.0.0.1:17333/ui/>**. Follow [Create your personal collection](docs/start-here.md#2-create-your-personal-collection), then [Store and recall a preference](docs/start-here.md#3-store-and-recall-a-preference): create a user key, retain a small preference, wait for indexing, and retrieve it with citations.

Your first success is a recalled preference whose citation leads to the original message. Then connect your agent and ask it to use that preference in a fresh session.

**[Complete first-memory walkthrough →](docs/start-here.md)**

## Connect Your Agent

Start the service and create a user key first. Client packages connect to OAM; they do not start the server.

| Agent or application | Integration |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code or Cursor | [MCP server and client configuration](integrations/mcp/README.md#client-configuration), Node.js 22+ |
| OpenClaw | [Plugin installation](integrations/openclaw/README.md#npm-installation), with automatic recall and eligible capture |
| DeepSeek Harness (DSH) | [DSH plugin](integrations/dsh/README.md) |
| Your own application | [Copyable HTTP example](docs/quickstart.md) and [API reference](docs/api.md) |

## See What Your Agent Remembers

![Memory Inspector showing recalled evidence and its original source](docs/assets/inspect-memory.png)

The Inspector lets you browse retained sources, inspect recalled memories and citations, manage Resources, and refresh your User Profile. This screenshot uses synthetic demonstration data. [Inspector guide](docs/memory-web-ui.md).

## How Memory Works

OAM preserves original conversations (**L0**), extracts source-backed facts (**L1**), and builds supported Insights across related facts (**L2**). A stored, refreshable User Profile (**L3**) helps the agent personalize its behavior. Text, HTML, PDF and image **Resources** remain separate evidence and can be retrieved alongside learned memory.

Recall supports **fast** and **normal** modes and returns cited context without generating the final answer. The default context limits are 18,000 and 24,000 tokens respectively. Your agent decides how to use that evidence and owns its final answer and total input budget.

[Memory and retrieval design](docs/indexing-retrieval.md) · [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) · [Configuration](configs/README.md)

## v0.2.0

**Updated BEAM-10M evaluation.** OAM earns 78.23% mean rubric credit versus Hindsight's published 64.08%, with 25 more passes across 200 questions and 9.85% fewer saved context tokens. This recorded comparison uses the same evaluation protocol with different models and memory pipelines. [Results and method](docs/benchmarks.md#3-beam-10m)

The release adds scheduled personal Profile refresh, custom Profiles generated on demand, and Insight consolidation across sources in a shared user window. Recall adds per-request preset overrides and optional personal-evidence selection.

See the [release notes](docs/releases/0.2.0.md) for verification and publication status. OpenClaw and DSH are independently versioned at 0.0.2. MCP is at 0.0.1.

## Documentation & Development

| Goal | Guide |
| --- | --- |
| Deploy or upgrade OAM | [Docker Compose](deploy/README.md) |
| Store and recall through HTTP | [Quickstart](docs/quickstart.md) · [API reference](docs/api.md) |
| Configure providers and operate the service | [Operations](docs/operations.md) |
| Understand verified behavior and limits | [Acceptance](docs/acceptance.md) · [Release notes](docs/releases/0.2.0.md) |
| Build, test or contribute | [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Release procedure](docs/releasing.md) |

Future work includes smoother onboarding, lower indexing and answer-context token usage, and shared Resource ownership. The Python SDK, hosted service, database high availability and OIDC/LDAP support remain future work. Share setup and retrieval feedback in [Discussions](https://github.com/rocke2020/open-agent-memory/discussions/1).

## Acknowledgments

OAM is informed by open-source work from [Hindsight](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight), [OpenViking](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking), [Mem0](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0), [MemOS](https://github.com/MemTensor/MemOS), [TencentDB Agent Memory](https://github.com/TencentCloud/TencentDB-Agent-Memory) and [gbrain](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain). We thank the [LongMemEval](https://github.com/xiaowu0162/LongMemEval) and [BEAM](https://github.com/mohammadtavakoli78/BEAM) authors and contributors. See [full acknowledgments](ACKNOWLEDGMENTS.md) and [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY.md).

## License

[Apache License 2.0](LICENSE).

# dsh-agent-browser

Native browser automation for [DSH](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh):
nine `browser_*` model tools driving [agent-browser](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser)
(Chrome via CDP), plus a live-view panel baked into the DSH web GUI — watch the
page the agent is working on, hold human takeover, and drive it yourself.

Part of a three-package family:

| package | role |
| --- | --- |
| **dsh-agent-browser** | DSH plugin: tools + panel (you are here) |
| [dsh-agent-browser-core](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-agent-browser-core) | daemon driver (JSON calls, streams, session registry) |
| [dsh-agent-browser-pi](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-agent-browser-pi) | pi extension at full tool parity |

## Install

Requires Node 24.9+, DSH 0.2.2 or newer with the web profile, and Chrome.
Tested against DSH `0.2.2-rc.1` (host tools + web client panel).
`agent-browser@0.43.0` uses installed system Chrome automatically; if none is
present, run the profile's `agent-browser install` once to fetch Chrome for
Testing.

**pnpm ≥ 10 gates dependency build scripts.** `agent-browser` ships one
(`postinstall` materializes the host-platform native binary from the matching
`@agent-browser/cli-*` optional dependency), so first allow it in the profile
you are installing into — once per profile:

```bash
printf '\nallowBuilds:\n  agent-browser: true\n' >> ~/.dsh/profiles/web/pnpm-workspace.yaml
```

then:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-agent-browser
```

Restart the DSH web profile and ask the agent to open a page — the panel
appears automatically. If the add step fails with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`,
the allowance above was not applied to that profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`
(interactive alternative: `cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web && pnpm approve-builds`).

> Note: 0.43 ships the native binary in per-platform `@agent-browser/cli-*`
> optional dependencies instead of the main tarball, so tools still work
> where lifecycle scripts stay blocked: the launcher materializes and links
> the platform binary on first run. Keep optional dependencies enabled (an
> `--omit=optional` / `optional=false` install leaves no binary to link); the
> allowance exists to satisfy default supply-chain policy and prepare the
> binary eagerly during install.

Uninstall: `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-agent-browser`.

## Tools

`browser_open`, `browser_snapshot`, `browser_find`, `browser_act`,
`browser_get`, `browser_eval`, `browser_screenshot`, `browser_tabs`,
`browser_session` — snapshot-ref discipline throughout (`act` returns
per-step outcomes plus a changed-region mini-snapshot), cookies redacted by
default, `eval` routed through the host approval seam.

## Panel

Canvas live view over the daemon's JPEG stream (ack-paced), session picker,
pin/pop-out, activity feed (console + URL events), and an explicit human-
takeover toggle — takeover input never routes through the model.

## Configuration

Row id `browser` in your profile patch, e.g.:

```yaml
- id: browser
  config:
    headed: false
    idleTimeoutMinutes: 30
    allowedDomains: ["example.com", "internal.corp"]
    autoOpenPanel: true
```

Off-list domains can be granted interactively per session through the host
approval flow when the agent tries to open them.

## License

MIT

## Local fork changes (DSH harness setup)

This copy is vendored by `Satont/dsh-harness-setup` and adds:

- the live panel defaults to the **right sidebar**, with a one-time localStorage migration
  from the old chip/float mode;
- the default `browser_*` session is keyed by the DSH conversation id
  (`exec.agent.session.id`), so each chat has its own page/tab context;
- the panel follows the active `uiSession` and hides for a chat without a live browser;
- the model prompt tells models to omit the optional `session` argument unless asked.

Keep these changes when upgrading the upstream package.

# DSH Harness Setup

A reproducible backup of a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) "Claude Code Desktop" style setup:
warm dark UI, GPT/Codex and other subscriptions as models, a visible agent browser
(any model can open, click and read pages while you watch inside DSH), project threads,
memory, artifacts with public sharing, session/worktree lifecycle, project skills and MCP,
and a phone-friendly HTTPS route through a small VPS.

This repository is a **template + runbook**, not a copy of the private DSH home.
No credentials, OAuth tokens, API keys, passwords or private account identifiers are
stored here. See [SECRETS.md](SECRETS.md) and [.env.example](.env.example).

## Status this backup was taken from

- DSH runtime: `0.2.3-alpha.2` (web profile, Node `26.13.1`)
- OS: Linux (Arch), Wayland, Node.js `26.13.1`
- Profile: `~/.dsh/profiles/web`
- UI: `dsh-claude-ui` (local CSS/client plugin)
- Main model: Codex subscription route `codex`, default `GPT-6.2-Sol`, medium effort
- Extra UI: `dsh-better-sidebar@0.32.0`, `dsh-context@0.85.1`,
  `dsh-plugin@2.3.9` (Plugin Hub), `@local/dsh-usage-limits` (Limits panel),
  `dsh-limits-strip` (local sidebar card), `whale-girl` Russian pet
- Voice: `dsh-voice-hex` with local Hex **Whisper large-v3-turbo**, default language `ru`
- Browser: local `dsh-agent-browser` fork in `plugins/agent-browser` — `browser_*` tools for
  every model + live viewport docked in the right sidebar; per-chat page context; managed
  Chrome via `agent-browser install`
- Subagents: model selection enabled for new Sessions; Kimi K3/K3.1 Pro route
  (`kimi-coding`) plus the default DeepSeek route
- Google Antigravity ACP: `dsh-bundle-antigravity-host@0.1.46` — official `agy` ACP
  agent, Gemini 4 Neon/Hydrogen families, OAuth in Settings → Antigravity ACP
- Extras: `impeccable` skill installed globally under `~/.dsh/skills/impeccable`

## What is in the repository

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | Instructions for the next agent: how to restore safely, what never to commit |
| `RESTORE.md` | Step-by-step restore, verification, and failure recovery |
| `profile/` | Profile manifests: `package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml`, pnpm settings |
| `plugins/` | Local plugin source: theme, inline bash, worktrees, limits card, patched agent browser |
| `ops/` | Desktop wrapper, mobile/VPS helpers, artifact sharing script, systemd units |
| `docs/` | Architecture, plugin inventory, VPS/mobile runbook, operations, secrets |
| `scripts/restore-profile.sh` | Build a fresh profile from this repo (backs up existing manifests) |
| `tools/model-tuning/` | Context-window and compaction tuning generator |

![Main UI](docs/screenshots/ui-dark.jpg)

| Limits page | Sidebar card |

![Mobile](docs/screenshots/mobile.jpg)

cropped where session names would appear. See `docs/screenshots/README.md`.

## Quick restore

```bash
git clone <this-repo> dsh-harness-setup
cd dsh-harness-setup
./scripts/restore-profile.sh web      # DSH_HOME defaults to ~/.dsh
dsh --profile web
```

Then open **Settings → Subscriptions** and sign in to ChatGPT/Codex (and optionally
Claude / Grok / Copilot / Antigravity). Sign-in tokens are stored outside this repo,
under `~/.dsh/plugins/subscriptions/auth.json`, never in git.

For the full procedure, including the VPS relay and the phone route, read
[RESTORE.md](RESTORE.md) and [docs/MOBILE-VPS.md](docs/MOBILE-VPS.md).

## Security model

- The repo contains **no live secrets**. Placeholders in `.env.example` must be filled
  locally or in a password manager.
- Public mobile access is HTTPS on your own VPS, protected by Traefik + Let's Encrypt
  and a Basic-Auth relay in front of the DSH launch-token/cookie flow. The home DSH
  server is not exposed directly.
- Public artifact pages are static snapshots served with a sandbox CSP; they do not
  receive DSH cookies or same-origin access.
- Do not commit `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`, `~/.dsh/plugins/subscriptions/auth.json`,
  `~/.config/dsh-mobile/vps.conf`, `dsh-mobile` runtime auth files, `.env`, SSH keys,
  or any token-bearing URL.

## License

Original scripts and documentation in this repository are MIT-licensed. Third-party
plugins under `plugins/` keep their own licenses and notices; see the files in each
plugin directory and `NOTICE` where present.

# dsh-threads

中文 | [English](README.en.md)

一个 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 插件，照着 Claude 的"项目 + 讨论串"做。项目的主对话当调度员：遇到能独立完成的任务，就开一个**讨论串**——一个你能点进去接着聊的真实会话；讨论串做完后，把简短的回报发回主对话。

> 状态：从 0.1.0 起是正式版，各个版本见 [Releases](https://github.com/Kyf-eng/dsh-threads/releases)。基于 DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2 开发，在 0.2.1-rc.2、0.2.1-rc.3 和 0.2.2-rc.1 上测试过。更新记录见 [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)，设计说明见 [docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md](docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md)。

![一条消息，主对话开出三条讨论串同时干活](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kyf-eng/dsh-threads/main/docs/media/demo.gif)

## 功能

- **项目**：一个文件夹 + 一个常驻主对话，有图标、给协调者的目标，以及所有讨论串也会收到的项目说明。在左侧"项目"里新建（用系统的文件夹选择器选文件夹），或者在会话的"…"菜单里选"设为项目"。卡片的"⋮"菜单可以置顶、归档、删除、设置这个项目的桌面通知，以及打开项目设置（协调器和讨论串的模型、使用情况）。
- **讨论串**：主对话为能独立完成的工作开讨论串、给讨论串追加指令，也会提出你没要求的建议（放在输入框上方的卡片里，你点了才开始）。每个讨论串都是真实会话：在右侧面板打开，直接和它对话。
- **回报**：讨论串回报做完了什么、改了哪些文件、要你决定什么。主对话只在它的讨论串都结束后被唤醒一次，并防止反复唤醒；忘了回报的讨论串会被提醒一次；讨论串留在后台的任务结束后补交的回报，也会送到主对话。
- **并行和隔离**：最多 3 个讨论串同时运行。会改文件的讨论串在自己的 git worktree 和分支（`dsh-threads/<n>-<id>`）里工作，不碰项目文件夹；你要求时主对话才合并，`/thread cleanup` 清理做完的 worktree。
- **Claude 式界面**：对话里的讨论串卡片、"↳ N 条回复"、等你回复时的举手、运行中的呼吸点、文件和分支小标签。左侧有单独的"项目"分组：每个项目一行（显示状态和 ↳N），点进去就是主对话。项目的主对话和讨论串都不出现在"工作区"列表里。

## 平台

- **macOS 桌面版**：主要的开发和测试平台，全部功能都实测过。
- **Windows 桌面版（x64）**：实测过两轮。项目、讨论串、worktree、清理、审批沿用、停止、归档和完整流程都正常。需要先装 [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win)；仓库路径很深时，见下面“排错”里的长路径。DeepSeek Harness 自己的 Windows 沙箱有时给不了项目文件夹写权限（`SetNamedSecurityInfoW failed (Win32 5)`），这时讨论串的终端命令要你一次性批准提权。桌面通知和英文界面还没在 Windows 上验证。
- **Linux**：DeepSeek Harness 没有 Linux 桌面版；Web 版在 Linux 上没测过。
- **Web 版**（`--profile web`）：在 macOS 上用过，没做完整测试。
- 单元测试在 Linux、macOS 和 Windows 的 CI 上都跑。

## 安装

需要 DeepSeek Harness **0.2.x**（桌面版或 Web 版；在 0.2.1-rc.2、0.2.1-rc.3 和 0.2.2-rc.1 上测试过）和它的 `dsh` 命令行。桌面版在应用菜单的"管理 dsh 命令…"里设置；没有这个命令时，可以用 npm 上和你的 DeepSeek Harness 同版本的命令行，例如 `npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.2 plugin --profile web add @kyf-eng/dsh-threads`。

1. 完全退出 DeepSeek Harness（macOS 上按 ⌘Q；有菜单栏或托盘图标的，也要从那里退出）。
2. 把插件加到你的 profile：

   ```sh
   dsh plugin --profile desktop add @kyf-eng/dsh-threads
   ```

   以后升级也是这一条命令（从 0.1.0-rc.7 及以后的预发布版升级到正式版也一样，项目和讨论串都保留）。Web 版用 `--profile web`。要装某个版本，在包名后面加 `@版本号`（例如 `@kyf-eng/dsh-threads@0.1.0`）；不想走 npm，也可以填 [Releases](https://github.com/Kyf-eng/dsh-threads/releases) 里那个 `.tgz` 的地址。
3. 启动 DeepSeek Harness，左侧出现"项目"。

卸载：`dsh plugin --profile desktop remove @kyf-eng/dsh-threads`（0.1.0-rc.6 及更早的版本叫 `@fky/dsh-threads`）。

从 0.1.0-rc.6 及更早的版本升级：包名从 `@fky/dsh-threads` 改成了 `@kyf-eng/dsh-threads`，新版本不会替换旧的。先完全退出 DeepSeek Harness，运行 `dsh plugin --profile desktop remove @fky/dsh-threads`，再按上面的第 2 步安装。项目和讨论串存在 DeepSeek Harness 自己的存储里，卸载旧包不会丢。

## 使用

1. **项目 → 新建项目**：起名，选一个文件夹（任意文件夹，还不是工作区的会自动添加）。
2. 在项目主对话里让它在后台做事（"开个讨论串去……"）。也可以输入 `/thread <任务>`，或 `/thread -w <任务>` 开一个有独立 worktree 的讨论串。
3. 点讨论串卡片，在右侧打开它，可以直接聊；运行中可以点"停止"（或 `/thread stop <n>`），做完了点"标记已解决"，不再需要的可以归档（已归档的单独列在最下面，可以取消归档）。
4. 模型提出建议时，在输入框上方的卡片里开始一个、全部开始或都不要。
5. worktree 讨论串的改动在它自己的分支上。自己合并或让主对话合并，然后 `/thread cleanup`（再 `/thread cleanup confirm`）。

## 配置

在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`（桌面版是 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml`）里给插件加 `config`：

```yaml
- id: dsh-threads
  config:
    maxRunning: 2
```

| 配置项 | 默认值 | 含义 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maxRunning` | 3 | 一个主对话同时能跑几个讨论串 |
| `maxAutoWakes` | 5 | 连续自动唤醒几次后，回报改为等你开口（0 表示从不自动唤醒） |
| `noteMaxChars` | 400 | 发回主对话的回报最长多少字 |
| `summaryMaxChars` | 300 | 讨论串摘要最长多少字 |
| `proposalTtlDays` | 7 | 没开始的建议几天后过期 |
| `maxProposalsPerTurn` | 3 | 模型一次最多提几个建议 |
| `reportReminder` | true | 讨论串做完任务却没回报时，提醒它一次 |
| `inheritPermissionPreset` | true | 讨论串沿用主对话的权限模式 |
| `offerApproval` | `ask` | 你只说了任务、没说要开讨论串时：`ask` 先弹确认卡（开讨论串 / 在主对话里做 / 先不做），`open` 不问直接开 |

## 排错

- **开着"开发者工具"时 DeepSeek Harness 崩溃**，日志里有 `inspector: source state exceeds the source-frame byte limit`：这是 DSH 实验性检查器的问题，插件多的 profile 都可能碰到。在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 末尾加下面一段，把单帧上限调到 1MB（要连 `captureFetch: true` 一起写）。**不要**点崩溃对话框里的"禁用第三方插件"，那会把所有第三方插件一起禁掉。

  ```yaml
  - id: experimental-inspector
    config:
      captureFetch: true
      maxSourceFrameBytes: 1048576
  ```

- **开 worktree 讨论串时提示“找不到 git”**：DeepSeek Harness 自己不带 git，用的是系统 PATH 里的 `git`。Windows 上装 [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win)（其他程序自带的 git 不算），然后完全退出并重开 DeepSeek Harness，让它读到新的 PATH。提示里引用了 git 的原话（比如 Windows 上的 `detected dubious ownership`）时，按 git 说的处理。

- **Windows 上开 worktree 提示路径太长**：worktree 放在仓库里的 `.agents\worktrees\…` 下，路径比原仓库长四十来个字符，仓库本身路径就很深时会超过 Windows 默认的 260 字符上限（git 报 `Filename too long`）。可以只为这个仓库打开长路径支持（`git -C <仓库> config core.longpaths true`），或者把仓库放到更短的路径下。

- **收不到桌面通知**：DeepSeek Harness 在前台时不发通知（侧栏的记号已经够了）。在后台也收不到时，看系统的通知设置：macOS 是"系统设置 → 通知 → DeepSeek Harness"，Windows 是"设置 → 系统 → 通知"，Linux 取决于桌面环境的通知服务。Web 版第一次会请求浏览器的通知权限。

## 已知限制

- DeepSeek Harness 每个工作区默认只列 5 个会话，隐藏的讨论串也算在里面，所以讨论串多的工作区里可见的行会变少，"展开其余 N 个会话"的 N 也包含讨论串。
- worktree 从文件夹最后一次提交开出：没提交的改动不在里面，依赖（`node_modules` 等）要在 worktree 里重新装。
- 没有花费上限：除了同时运行的数量，讨论串用多少 token 不设限。用量在项目设置的"使用情况"里看。

## 开发

需要 Node ≥ 22.19。

```sh
npm install
npm run check
# 完全退出 DeepSeek Harness 后：
npm run dev:install
```

`dev:install` 默认用 macOS 桌面版自带的 `dsh`。其他安装方式用 `DSH_CLI=<dsh 命令的路径> npm run dev:install`，`DSH_PROFILE` 指定 profile（默认 `desktop`）。约定和测试方法见 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)。

## 协议

MIT

# dsh-voice-hex

DSH speech-to-text providers backed by the local [Hex](https://github.com/anomalyco/hex)
dictation app. One provider is registered for every model Hex reports, so the existing
microphone button in the composer gets a provider picker:

- Hex · Whisper large-v3-turbo (multilingual, Russian; the recommended default)
- Hex · Parakeet v3 / unified English
- Hex · Qwen3-ASR 0.6B
- Hex · SenseVoice Small
- Hex · GigaAM v3 (Russian)
- …plus the rest of the Hex model list

Audio never leaves the machine: the browser records a WAV, DSH's speech service passes it
to this host plugin, and the plugin runs:

```bash
hex transcribe --json --model <hex-model-id> --language <lang> <recording.wav>
```

The transcript is inserted into the composer draft, exactly like the built-in local
SenseVoice provider.

## Requirements

- Hex 3.4+ installed and running (or at least its models installed)
- Hex Labs › **Transcribe files** enabled once:

```bash
hex labs on transcribe-files
```

- The selected model must be installed in Hex. Models that are not installed appear in
  the DSH provider list with a **Download and prepare** action; that action runs
  `hex model install <id>` and restores Hex's previously selected model afterwards.

## Install into a DSH profile

```bash
pnpm add file:plugins/voice-hex
```

The package's `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the `voice-hex` row. Then select a provider in
DSH **Plugins → Voice Input → Speech recognition** (or keep the profile default
`hex-whisper-large-v3-turbo` and language `ru`).

The profile override used by this setup:

```yaml
- id: speech-to-text
  config:
    defaultProvider: hex-whisper-large-v3-turbo
    language: ru
```

## Config

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `command` | `hex` | Hex CLI binary or absolute path |
| `timeoutMs` | `180000` | Per-transcription timeout |

No API key is used. Hex's own service authentication stays inside Hex; this plugin only
uses the local CLI.

## Verification

```bash
hex model list --json            # find whisper_large_v3_turbo
hex labs on transcribe-files
hex transcribe --json --model whisper_large_v3_turbo --language ru /tmp/test.wav
```

Then click the microphone in DSH, say something, and press Stop. The transcript should
appear in the draft; no session message is sent until you press Send.
